question: I am building a detached single-family house in Partille in an area where the detaljplan allows detached single-family houses. I want to add a frontispiece on one roof slope and a broad dormer on the other; both would rise above the eaves, and the dormer would have essentially the same design as the frontispiece. The roof changes would add about 37 sqm of gross floor area through increased volume, although about 12 sqm is newly measurable area; the dormer would span about 10 metres of a 20.7-metre roof slope and require changes to the primary load-bearing structure. Can these roof additions be carried out as building-permit-exempt measures?
key_points: Under PBL 1 kap. 4 §, a tillbyggnad is a change that increases a building’s volume; under PBL 9 kap. 4 b §, the volume increase must not exceed 15 sqm of bruttoarea, rather than counting only newly measurable area.
A building-permit-exempt takkupa under PBL 9 kap. 4 b § must meet the statutory limits, including occupying no more than half the roof slope and causing no intervention in the load-bearing structure.

The distinction between a takkupa and a frontespis depends on whether the construction is part of the roof or the façade; a structure projecting above the eaves is a frontespis, and a similarly designed structure is not exempt as a takkupa.
The assessment of a permit-exempt alteration must be made against a completed building approved for use by a slutbesked or qualifying interim slutbesked.

outcome: MÖD annulled the startbesked for the frontispiece and dormer because neither qualified for the claimed building-permit exemptions, but left the startbesked for creating an additional dwelling in force.

question: I want to build an approximately 80-square-metre holiday home on my property in Nynäshamn, which already has a holiday home and a small outbuilding. An earlier shoreline-protection exemption for the outbuilding designated the whole property as the plot. The proposed building site is wooded, undeveloped land outside the existing home’s privacy zone, and the property includes both land and water.
key_points: Under MB 7 kap. 18 c § first paragraph 1, a special reason requires the site to have already been taken into use in a way that makes it insignificant to shoreline-protection purposes.
A tomtplats designation is tied to the purpose of the original exemption and does not, by itself, extinguish public access rights throughout the designated area.
A new, independent dwelling is not a supplementary measure supported by the existing home’s tomtplats; the existing home’s need for a plot is the relevant starting point.
Because the proposed site was outside the existing home’s privacy zone and was not otherwise taken into use, the court found no special reason for an exemption.

question: Can I obtain a building permit in Norra Sköndal, Stockholm, to build two noise barriers, about 370 and 200 metres long, on top of an existing noise berm beside road 229? The barriers would stand on land designated as parkland in detailed plans whose implementation periods have expired, near existing homes; the berm was built around 1970. The plans concern residential development, and the barriers are intended to reduce traffic noise in connection with road and bus-stop works; alternative locations and noise-reduction measures have been considered.
key_points: Under PBL 9 kap. 31 b § 1, an extensive departure placing long barriers on parkland is not a minor deviation, even if compatible with the plan’s purpose.
PBL 9 kap. 31 b § 2 did not apply because the need for noise protection had been anticipated when the plans were implemented and the berm was built.

After the implementation period has expired, PBL 9 kap. 31 c § 1 can allow a deviation that is compatible with the plan’s purpose and meets an urgent shared need; the barriers were materially important to homes along the road.

A supplementary suitability assessment is required, including weighing other interests and considering alternative solutions; the court accepted the evidence that alternatives would not adequately meet the noise-reduction need.
The project also had to meet PBL 2 kap. 6 § and not cause a significant nuisance under PBL 2 kap. 9 §; the court found those requirements satisfied.

outcome: MÖD held that the barriers were compatible with the plans’ purpose and met an urgent shared need, and upheld the building permit under PBL 9 kap. 31 c § 1.

question: I want to build a single-family house and garage on my already developed property in Mossbystrand, Skurup, near road 9. The proposed site is open land within an area that the detailed comprehensive plan identifies as existing residential development where densification may be possible; it is agricultural land classified as class 4 and borders a larger area of farmland. The site is outside the areas affected by shoreline protection and landscape protection.
key_points: A förhandsbesked under PBL 9 kap. 17 § assesses whether the proposed measure may be permitted at the chosen location.
Under MB 3 kap. 4 §, productive agricultural land may be used for development only if needed for a substantial societal interest and that need cannot be met satisfactorily by using other land.
The need for alternative-location evidence is concrete: alternatives must be assessed as acceptable from a community-planning perspective.

A detailed comprehensive plan can support the alternative-location assessment when it clearly identifies suitable areas for development and shows how agricultural land and other constraints were considered.
Here, the property lay within a narrowly identified area where densification was contemplated, while much of the surrounding area was excluded to protect agricultural land.

question: I live in a group-built detached-house area in Järfälla, on a corner plot beside shared residential land used by pedestrians, cyclists and some other traffic. An existing 13 m² accessory building would be replaced by a 30 m² building, set back somewhat from the boundary but within 4.5 metres of it; the samfällighetsförening that owns the adjoining land agrees to the location. The detailed plan designates the adjoining land for residential use, and smaller accessory buildings in the area are generally placed back from boundaries. Can I receive a startbesked for the proposed building?
key_points: A building-loavenged accessory building under PBL 9 kap. 4 a § is not an unconditional building right; it must still meet applicable PBL requirements.
A startbesked for a notification-required measure may be issued only if the building committee finds that the measure meets the applicable requirements under PBL 10 kap. 23 §.
PBL 2 kap. 6 § requires attention to the site and the interest of a good overall effect; the building’s placement and design must be assessed in the context of the existing environment.

Traffic effects must be considered under PBL 2 kap. 6 § even when adjoining land is designated as residential land rather than a street in the detailed plan; here, the reduced visibility was not by itself sufficiently established as grounds for refusal.

question: I want to build a 238 m² detached house on my plot on Svärdsön near Saltsjöbaden in Nacka, outside a detailed development plan and within 300 metres of the shoreline. A small cottage that previously stood on the plot was demolished several years ago, and there is now a small outbuilding; the plot is excluded from the surrounding nature reserve, though the reserve borders it. The terrain near the shore is steep, and I have a separate, final shoreline-protection exemption for the proposed house. Can I obtain building permission?
key_points: Outside a detailed development plan, PBL 9 kap. 31 § requires the proposal to meet the applicable requirements in PBL 2 kap.
Under PBL 2 kap. 4 §, land may be built on only if it is suitable for the purpose from a public-interest perspective.
A building-permit review is independently conducted, but it cannot, on the same evidence, overturn a final shoreline-protection exemption by rejecting the assessment made in that exemption case.
A shoreline-protection location can be relevant to the PBL suitability assessment, but a separate final exemption must be given significant weight where the assessments overlap.
The plot’s exclusion from the nature reserve and its prior development were relevant to the court’s conclusion that the reserve’s impact did not prevent this building permission.

question: We have built a detached house in Nässjö, and the electrical panel is positioned so that its upper switches are about 185 cm above the floor. Our control plan calls for the panel controls to be placed about 80–110 cm above floor level, but we have not found any specific regulation on electrical-panel height. Can the municipality make the final notice depend on moving the panel?
key_points: Under PBL 8 kap. 1 §, buildings must be suitable for their purpose and accessible and usable for people with reduced mobility or orientation, but this general requirement does not prescribe specific equipment or dimensions.

Under PBL 8 kap. 4 §, technical-property requirements must be essential; the court found accessibility to an electrical panel non-essential because it has a passive function and is not used regularly.
Under PBL 8 kap. 4 § and 16 kap. 2 § 3, the detailed meaning of technical-property requirements is set by regulations; no such regulations govern the placement of electrical panels.
Under PBL 8 kap. 4 a §, a municipality may not impose additional technical-property requirements beyond those in the law or regulations, and an unsupported additional requirement has no effect.
A final notice could not be made conditional under PBL 10 kap. 36 § on relocating the panel to a specified height when that requirement lacked support in the planning and building rules.
outcome: MÖD dismissed the municipality’s appeal, holding that the panel-height requirement was an unsupported municipal technical requirement and could not be made a condition of the final notice.

question: Our logistics property in Kungens kurva, Huddinge, has an existing gate used for frequent daily deliveries. The gate opens outward across a pedestrian and cycle path that the municipality has built alongside the property in accordance with the detailed plan; when open, it blocks the entire pedestrian path and half the cycle path. Can we keep using the gate in this configuration?
key_points: Under PBL 11 kap. 22 §, a building work within a detailed-plan area may be subject to an order if changed conditions make it a major traffic-safety nuisance.

A gate that, when open, blocks the whole pedestrian path and half the cycle path can constitute a major traffic-safety nuisance, particularly when frequent deliveries mean it is open for much of the day.
The required measure need only remedy or reduce the nuisance; changing the gate so it does not open outward was sufficient.
The fact that the municipality created the changed conditions by building the path did not prevent an order under PBL 11 kap. 22 §.

outcome: MÖD upheld the order requiring the owner to change the gate so that it does not open outward over the pedestrian and cycle path.

question: I want to establish a large riding facility in the rural Flyinge area, with riding arenas, a riding route and raised earthworks made from imported excavated material. The land is near existing homes and is subject to local area regulations intended to protect the landscape; it is open land rather than an existing residential plot. What permits would these works require?
key_points: PBF 6 kap. 1 § 1 contains an exhaustive list of permit-required facilities; an idrottsanläggning is not automatically an idrottsplats.
PBL 16 kap. 7 § authorises rules requiring permits for facilities with significant effects, but significant size or impact alone does not make an unlisted facility permit-required.
PBL 9 kap. 13 § 2 and the applicable area regulations did not require a land permit for these earthworks because the affected land was not tomtmark covered by those provisions.
A prior land permit had become final and could not be reviewed in this case; the municipality was not required to take further action regarding the facility.
outcome: MÖD held that the riding facility was not a permit-required idrottsplats and that the earthworks did not require a land permit under the area regulations, so no further PBL intervention was warranted.
source: MÖD 2022:13 (P 8384-21, 2022-09-14): Fråga om bygglovsplikt för ridanläggning

question: I want to build a single-family house and garage on an undeveloped plot of about 0.5 hectares in a rural area of Umeå municipality. Houses lie to the north and south, a small wooded area lies to the east, and a private road runs along the west; part of the plot has been used as a sports field for decades, and the rest has not been actively farmed for a long time. The plot is small and awkwardly shaped, but lies beside a road and near agricultural land that is still farmed.
key_points: A förhandsbesked under PBL 9 kap. 17 § addresses whether the proposed measure can be allowed at the specified location; the land must be suitable under PBL 2 kap. and 9 kap. 31 §.
Under MB 3 kap. 4 §, valuable agricultural land may be used for development only where the stated substantial public-interest and alternative-location requirements are met.
Whether land is valuable for cultivation must be assessed over the long term; past non-use and lack of economic practicality alone do not settle the question.

Here, the plot’s small size, poor layout and long period without active cultivation supported the finding that it was not valuable agricultural land, despite its access to a road and proximity to land still farmed.

outcome: MÖD overturned the lower court and reinstated the municipality’s positive preliminary decision, finding that the plot was not arable agricultural land of value for cultivation and that no other obstacle to the decision had been shown.

question: I want to redevelop a block at Stureplan in central Östermalm, where the existing buildings include a gallery, a former car hall and other buildings with cultural-historical value; some are green-classified by the city museum. The project would demolish parts of the existing development, rebuild some street-facing façades, add new buildings and allow taller rooftop additions and mixed uses. The area is within the national interest for the cultural environment of Stockholm inner city with Djurgården.
key_points: Under MB 3 kap. 6 §, areas of national interest for cultural heritage must be protected from measures that may cause significant harm; the test is whether the plan causes such harm to the interest.
The impact on the national interest must be assessed for the demolitions and height increases separately, together, and in combination with the plan’s other measures.
Under PBL 2 kap. 3 §, planning must promote appropriate development with regard to natural and cultural values and environmental and climate aspects.
Under PBL 2 kap. 6 §, the design and placement of buildings must take account of cultural values and the character of the surrounding built environment.

outcome: MÖD dismissed the appeals and upheld the detailed plan in full, finding that the permitted demolitions and increased building heights would not cause significant harm to the national cultural-environment interest.

question: Can a detailed plan for two apartment buildings with about 50 homes on natural land in Västertorp be validly adopted? The adoption decision refers to the city planning office’s service memorandum, whose footer lists a plan map and other documents as appendices, but those documents are not included in the memorandum. No new map was prepared after the review stage, and the earlier map is linked to the memorandum through the municipality’s internal case-management system.
key_points: Under PBL 4 kap. 30 §, a detaljplan must consist of a map of the area covered by the plan and the necessary provisions.
Under Kommunallagen 5 kap. 67 §, the protocol must record the decisions made in each matter; the decision’s content must be ascertainable from the protocol or documents it refers to.
A reference in a memo’s footer to appendices does not identify the adopted map clearly when those appendices are not part of the memo or otherwise clearly incorporated into the decision.
A map linked to a memo only through the municipality’s internal case-management system is not enough to establish which map was adopted.

evidence.contains: ska bestå av en karta över det område

outcome: MÖD annulled the adoption decision because the protocol did not make clear which plan map had been adopted, contrary to PBL 4 kap. 30 § and Kommunallagen 5 kap. 67 §.
source: MÖD 2022:5 (P 7791-21, 2022-03-29): Antagande av ny detaljplan

question: I own a forestry property of about 70 hectares in Kungsbacka, divided into several parcels, and want to subdivide about 22 hectares containing a house, farm buildings, about 13 hectares of arable and pasture land, and about 8 hectares of woodland. The subdivision is part of a family succession: some of my children plan to continue the forestry business, while another plans to run a smallholding with horses and sheep and use about 7 hectares of woodland for forest grazing; that woodland has previously been grazed and is difficult to access with forestry machinery.
key_points: Under FBL 3 kap. 7 §, forest land must not be divided in a way that significantly worsens the possibility of using the forest economically.
FBL 3 kap. 7 § also prohibits a division that would be harmful to a forestry property; assess the effect of the subdivision on the forestry property as a whole.
In applying FBL 3 kap. 7 §, the court considered the woodland’s limited value for active forestry, its inaccessibility, and its lack of connection to the more productive forest.

The intended change to forest grazing was relevant in light of the owner’s stated plans, the earlier grazing use, and authorities’ assessments that grazing was possible and could benefit nature values.

evidence.contains: möjligheten att ekonomiskt utnyttja skogen undergår försämring av någon betydelse

outcome: MÖD dismissed the County Administrative Board’s appeal, leaving the approved subdivision in place.
source: MÖD 2022:11 (F 1991-21, 2022-03-28): Fråga om skadlig delning av en skogsbruksfastighet i samband med avstyckning

question: I own a rural residential property in Piteå of about 1,370 square metres, with a house, and want to add roughly 3.9 hectares of adjoining agricultural land for small-scale cultivation and keeping hens and sheep. The land is part of a larger cultivated field and is currently farmed by a tenant; the property from which it would be transferred is about 73 hectares, mostly forest, with around 10 hectares of agricultural land. The area is outside a detailed development plan, and I want to keep the land open and use it alongside my home.
key_points: Under FBL 3 kap. 1 §, a newly formed or altered property must be permanently suitable for its intended purpose; MÖD found no obstacle under this general suitability test.

FBL 3 kap. 6 § protects agriculture only when the measure concerns an agricultural property; for a mixed forest-and-farm property, the dominant purpose and whether the agricultural part is viable or developable are relevant.
A property dominated by forestry, with about 10 hectares of agricultural land that was not sufficient to support viable or developable farming, was not an agricultural property under FBL 3 kap. 6 §.

Although FBL 3 kap. 3 § applies to property formation outside a detailed plan, it cannot be used to impose stronger protection for agricultural land than the specific agricultural-protection rules provide.

olägenhet av betydelse för jordbruksnäringen
skulle försvåra områdets ändamålsenliga användning

outcome: MÖD set aside the lower court’s decision and upheld the land-survey authority’s approval of the transfer because the source property was not an agricultural property for FBL purposes and the general suitability rules did not prevent the measure.

question: Can I obtain a building permit in Vellinge for a three-level apartment building, with the top level arranged as an attic? The detailed plan allows a maximum building height of 7.5 metres and no more than two storeys, while allowing dormers and elevator overruns in addition to that height. The design includes tall frontispieces extending across a substantial part of the façade; the proposed building is about 37.6 metres from a neighbouring villa.
key_points: Under PBF 1 kap. 3 §, building height is measured using the relevant façade plane and a plane angled 45 degrees inward; frontispieces may affect that calculation when their size and design make the building appear higher.
A detailed-plan exception for dormers does not apply to frontispieces: a dormer is part of the roof, while a frontispiece is part of the façade.
Under PBF 1 kap. 4 §, the attic counted as a storey because the building height was more than 0.7 metres above the upper surface of the attic-floor structure.
Under PBL 9 kap. 31 b §, neither the height deviation nor the excess storey was a minor deviation from the detailed plan; the plan description and illustrations did not override the plan provision.

outcome: MÖD revoked the building permit for House B because the frontispieces meant that the building exceeded the plan’s limits for both height and storeys, and neither deviation was minor.
source: MÖD 2022:4 (P 2153-21, 2022-02-23): Bygglov för flerbostadshus med frontespiser: beräkning av byggnadshöjd och våningsantal

question: In Gnesta, I own land that contains the whole of a shared road samfällighet, which is jointly owned with a neighbouring property. I want to transfer part of the samfällighet to my property because the road gets in the way of maintaining and using my buildings and parking area. The neighbour has made a new access road, although the shared road could be made usable for vehicle access.
key_points: Under FBL 5 kap. 4 §, a land transfer must lead to a more suitable property division or land use, with benefits outweighing its costs and disadvantages.
Under FBL 5 kap. 5 §, a transfer requested by an owner must be necessary to improve a property belonging to the applicant.
Under FBL 5 kap. 8 §, the resulting property must remain suitable for its intended use and must not suffer a substantial reduction in grading value or cause considerable inconvenience to its owner.

A compulsory transfer must also satisfy all three limbs of proportionality under RF 2 kap. 15 §; the assessment must account for the public interests underlying FBL, not just the private interests of the parties.
MÖD did not decide whether the road transfer met those requirements; it remitted the issue so the land survey authority could assess FBL first and then, if needed, proportionality.

outcome: MÖD set aside the decisions concerning transfer of the road area and sent that question back to the land survey authority for further assessment under FBL and, if relevant, a full proportionality review; it upheld the refusal to transfer the separate triangular area.

question: In Ronneby, I want to build a preschool on an undeveloped site in a residential area, between existing housing areas. The 1964 building plan marks the site for general public purposes, and its plan description suggests use for a small school, but the site has not previously been built on or used for a school. I am applying through a privately owned company.
key_points: Under PBL 9 kap. 32 a §, a private applicant may seek a building permit for land designated for a public purpose, subject to the statutory limits when that purpose is not specified in the plan.
A purpose mentioned only in the plan description does not count as being specified in the plan when it is absent from the plan map and provisions.
Where the public purpose is not specified, the rule for a private applicant ties permission to the site's latest use or a minor deviation from its latest or intended use.
An undeveloped site with no previous use cannot meet that use-based test for a proposed preschool.

outcome: MÖD overturned the building permit and rejected the application because the plan did not specify the public purpose in its map or provisions and the undeveloped site had no prior use that could satisfy the rule for a private applicant.

question: I own a single-family house in Professorsstaden in Lund and want to install solar panels on three roof slopes visible from the street. The house is in a neighbourhood identified in the conservation programme as part of a culturally valuable environment, and the detailed plan designates the area for special environmental consideration. The panels would be mounted on the existing roof.
key_points: Under PBL 8 kap. 13 §, a building in a particularly valuable built environment may not be altered in a way that distorts the environment’s distinctive character; the house was considered part of such an environment.
Under PBL 8 kap. 17 §, alterations must be carried out carefully with regard to the building’s character; the proposed panels’ design did not meet that requirement.

The visibility of the roof slopes from the street and the conservation designations in the detailed plan and conservation programme supported the assessment that the panels would distort the environment.
Under PBL 2 kap. 1 §, the balance between public and private interests favoured the public interest in preservation; the asserted climate benefits did not change the result.
outcome: MÖD dismissed the appeal and refused building permission for the panels on the street-visible roof slopes because they would contravene the alteration and heritage-protection requirements in PBL 8 kap. 13 and 17 §§.
source: MÖD 2021:21 (P 10501-20, 2021-11-09): Bygglov för solcellspaneler

question: We want to prepare a detailed plan for about 15 holiday or permanent homes beside Lake Stora Le in a sparsely developed rural area. The site is within a LIS area identified in the municipality’s comprehensive plan, but lies within the 100-metre shoreline protection zone; the proposed homes would be about 25–35 metres from the shore, with parts of the area left undeveloped. By car, the site is about 22 minutes from Töcksfors, 11 minutes from Holmedal school and 25 minutes from Årjäng, and the lake area is designated of national interest for nature conservation and outdoor recreation.
key_points: Under MB 7 kap. 18 d §, LIS-related grounds for lifting shoreline protection may apply when development can contribute to rural development.
A municipality’s LIS designation will normally be sufficient where the county administrative board raised no objection, but the circumstances of the individual case still matter.
There is no general acceptable-distance rule for homes intended to strengthen service; assess the local context and actual travel distances.
Even within a LIS area, lifting shoreline protection through a detailed plan requires special grounds and must be assessed against the purposes of shoreline protection.
outcome: MÖD rejected the appeal and upheld the detailed plan, finding the service distances acceptable in the circumstances and special grounds for lifting shoreline protection.
source: MÖD 2021:24 (P 10444-20, 2021-10-06): LIS-område i detaljplan

question: I want to build a 24-metre telecommunications mast and two equipment huts on park land in Kälvesta, Stockholm, near a road and about ten metres from garage buildings. The 1973 detailed plan designates the site as park, and I need the site to improve mobile coverage after losing access to an existing installation; nearby development plans and coverage constraints limit the alternatives.
key_points: Under PBL 2 kap. 6 §, buildings must be suitably designed and placed with regard to the townscape, landscape, natural and cultural values, and overall coherence.

Under PBL 9 kap. 31 c §, after the plan implementation period has expired, a plan-deviating permit may be granted if the measure is consistent with the plan's purpose and serves an urgent common need or public interest.
Applying PBL 9 kap. 31 c § also requires a supplementary suitability assessment that weighs the competing interests, including whether the purpose could be achieved at another location.
The applicant should support the proposed location with evidence about coverage needs and feasible alternatives; the court found Telia's explanation and coverage map adequate.
A municipality opposing a plan-deviating measure should give sufficiently weighty and legitimate reasons; its objection did not outweigh the public interest and location evidence in this case.

outcome: MÖD set aside the refusal and returned the case to the committee for continued handling, finding that the application could be granted under PBL 9 kap. 31 c §.

question: Can I build a sports hall for events with up to 3,300 spectators, together with dining and office space, and a four-storey parking structure with 159 spaces in Linköping? The site is on land designated for public purposes in a 1961 stadsplan; it was most recently used for temporary school barracks and before that as a ball field, with some parking also taking place there. A smaller sports hall already stands elsewhere in the area covered by the stadsplan.
key_points: Under PBL 9 kap. 32 a §, a non-public applicant may obtain a permit on land designated for a public purpose, but where that purpose is not specified in the plan, the proposed use must match the public-purpose use most recently made of the site or be a minor deviation from it.
Under PBL 9 kap. 32 a §, assess the part of the property covered by the relevant plan and proposed for development; uses elsewhere on the property do not establish the site’s most recent use.
A new large event venue was not the same use as temporary school barracks or a ball field; the existing smaller sports hall elsewhere did not make the new hall a minor addition.

Occasional parking on the site did not make a four-storey parking structure the same use, and the development’s increased traffic and visual impact supported finding that it was not a minor deviation under PBL 9 kap. 32 a §.

outcome: MÖD set aside the building permits and refused both applications because the proposed development was neither the same public-purpose use as the site’s most recent use nor a minor deviation from it.
source: MÖD 2021:13 (P 6977-20, 2021-09-06): Bygglov på s.k. A-tomt när sökanden inte är ett offentligt organ

question: I want to build a detached single-family house in Öckerö, where the detailed development plan allows buildings with at most two storeys. The design includes an upper tower enclosed by walls and a roof, with a floor covering more than half its area and an opening in the middle down to the storey below. Would this design qualify for building permission?
key_points: Under PBL 9 kap. 30 §, building permission within a detailed-plan area requires the proposal to comply with the detailed plan.
A storey is assessed by the building’s technical construction; its outward appearance alone is not decisive.
A storey need not have a floor covering its entire area: the tower’s partial floor and potential for use meant it counted as a storey.
Because the plan limited buildings to two storeys, the house’s three storeys breached the plan, and the deviation was not acceptable.

outcome: MÖD dismissed the appeal, finding that the tower counted as a third storey and that the resulting conflict with the detailed plan could not be accepted.

question: I want to build a multifamily building in Skälby, where there is currently a single-family house built in 1963 and the roads and municipal water and sewer have been provided. The area is covered by an older subdivision plan from 1927. A county board order from 1952 prohibited new construction until water and sewer had been provided sufficiently, and I do not know of an express decision repealing that order.
key_points: Under 17 kap. 4 § ÄPBL, an avstyckningsplan covered by a 168 § Building Act order ceased to apply when ÄPBL took effect; otherwise it continued as a detailed plan.

A conditional order under 109 and 168 §§ of the Building Act prohibiting new construction until water and sewer were sufficiently provided ended automatically when that condition was fulfilled; no separate repeal decision was required.
The court found that water and sewer had been provided sufficiently in the area by January 1963 at the latest, so no 168 § order remained in force when ÄPBL took effect.

Because the avstyckningsplan continued as a detailed plan, the permit application must be assessed under PBL 9 kap. 30 §; MÖD did not decide whether the proposed multifamily building satisfies that provision.
outcome: MÖD dismissed the municipality’s appeal, held that the conditional building prohibition had ended when its infrastructure condition was met and the subdivision plan continued as a detailed plan, and required the building-permit application to be reconsidered under PBL 9 kap. 30 §.
source: MÖD 2021:7 (P 4230-20, 2021-05-31): Villkorat förordnande om byggnadsförbud

question: We have an on-site wastewater facility serving a home in Värmdö, for WC and household wastewater, and it was installed under a municipal permit granted in 2004. The municipality inspected it and identified functional problems, including missing phosphorus treatment, and is considering prohibiting discharge. The property also has an accessory building, and the permit documents show both buildings, although the connection from the accessory building is not marked on the plan. Can the municipality prohibit discharge from the facility?
key_points: Under MB 24 kap. 1 §, a final permit binds all parties regarding the matters examined in the permit decision.
Where a permit was granted after an environmental-code assessment, additional requirements based on the general consideration rules cannot be imposed for matters already examined.
Under MB 26 kap. 9 § third paragraph, an injunction or prohibition may not restrict a permit that has legal force under MB 24 kap. 1 §.

A municipality may supervise compliance with permit conditions and may order corrective action for breaches; changes or additions to the facility may instead require reconsideration under MB 24 kap. 5 §.
The permit’s scope matters: whether discharge from an accessory building is covered may require further examination of the application and permit documents.

outcome: MÖD dismissed the municipality’s appeal, holding that the 2004 permit’s legal force prevented it from prohibiting discharge based on additional requirements for matters covered by that permit.

question: I am building a detached one-family house in Vallentuna and want to furnish an additional dwelling, add a 15 m² extension and two dormers, and build a 25 m² accessory dwelling. The house has an interim final certificate, and the whole building has been allowed to be used. Can I get start notices for these measures before the house has received a final final certificate or been completed for several years?
key_points: PBL 9 kap. 4 a–c §§ exempts certain measures at a one- or two-family house from building-permit requirements, including an additional dwelling and an accessory dwelling, subject to the statutory conditions.

A measure such as an extension must relate to an existing one- or two-family house; the relevant test is whether the house is sufficiently complete for the measure to naturally count as an extension or a complement.

Under PBL 10 kap. 36 §, an interim final certificate together with a decision allowing the whole house to be used can satisfy that test; a final final certificate is not required in these circumstances.
The PBL does not require the house to have held a final certificate for five years before these building-permit-exempt measures can receive start notices.
outcome: MÖD dismissed the appeals and upheld the start notices, finding the interim final certificate and permission to use the whole house sufficient in these circumstances.

question: I have notified the authorities that I want to harvest trees in a forest area on my land in Härryda, including some birches for firewood and a large oak beside my cottage that I consider hazardous. Frogs are known from a nearby pond, but I have not seen frogs or lesser spotted woodpeckers on my land. Can I carry out the planned harvesting?
key_points: A notification of forest harvesting is treated as a consultation notification under MB 12 kap. 6 §.
Under MB 12 kap. 6 §, the authority may require precautions to limit or prevent harm to the natural environment, or prohibit the activity when necessary.
The decision concerns an interim prohibition, not a final determination that the remaining harvesting is permanently impermissible.
The oak was excepted from the prohibition; the rest of the notified harvesting remained barred while the interim order applied.

outcome: MÖD allowed the landowner to remove the large oak but otherwise upheld the interim prohibition on harvesting.

question: We own two properties in Tyresö that are included in a detailed plan reserving land for shared facilities, including a road and water and sewer lines. The municipality has applied to establish shared facilities for the properties and to transfer land from municipal land into a common property. The properties are within the municipal public water-and-sewer service area; after a final decision, connection points are to be located at the property boundaries, with public pipes brought there, although the originally proposed points were more than 70 metres away.
key_points: Under AL 6 a §, the AL 5 and 6 §§ conditions are not applied to a shared facility established during the detailed plan’s implementation period when the plan provides for it.

Under AL 7 §, a shared facility must not be established when participating owners generally oppose it and have weighty reasons; the public pipes reaching the property boundaries meant there was no longer a need for the shared water-and-sewer facility.

Under FBL 5 kap. 5 §, a requested property adjustment generally must be necessary to improve the applicant’s property; the municipality’s land transfer did not improve its property and was not necessary to manage the road facility.

The detailed plan’s exception to the FBL improvement requirement applies only when the adjustment is needed to bring a property into better conformity with the plan; that exception did not apply to this land transfer.
The shared road facility remained permissible because the conditions for establishing it under AL were met.

mera allmänt motsätter sig åtgärden och har beaktansvärda skäl för det

outcome: MÖD upheld the shared road facility but set aside the common-property formation and the shared water-and-sewer facility, and adjusted the allocation of costs.

question: Can we adopt a detailed plan for about 160 apartments on a cleared former industrial site in Kungsängen, roughly 350 metres’ walking distance from the commuter-train station? The land is covered by a 1933 building plan for industrial or commercial use and was not previously subject to shoreline protection. Our proposal keeps shoreline protection on parkland closest to the water, with public access via a planned square; we have assessed alternative sites within 700 metres of the station. Nearby homes include villas and apartment buildings, and residents may be affected by changes to their views and privacy.
key_points: Under MB 7 kap. 18 c § first paragraph, point 5, housing that serves an important public interest may justify lifting shoreline protection if that interest cannot be met outside the protected area; the alternatives investigation must be adequate and the exception is applied restrictively.

Under PBL 4 kap. 17 §, the public interest in the planned use must outweigh the shoreline-protection interest; the balance depends on the circumstances, including previous land use and whether accessible protected parkland remains by the water.

Under PBL 2 kap. 9 §, a plan must not cause significant nuisance; assess effects such as loss of views, overlooking and reduced light in light of the area’s character and what residents could reasonably expect.
Under PBL 4 kap. 36 §, a detailed plan must give reasonable consideration to existing building, ownership and property conditions.
A remittal means the plan’s ultimate validity remains unresolved where other objections have not yet been decided.

question: I own a property by Osbysjön in Osby, within a bird protection area and close to the shoreline. It was formerly used as a guesthouse, and a fence, stone table, grill place and dock were already present when I bought it; the dock has been there for nearly 40 years, and an older dock was nearby before that. Can I keep these features and continue cutting vegetation in the area by the water?
key_points: Under MB 26 kap. 12 §, an order against a new owner to remedy a prior owner's shoreline-protection violation requires an assessment of whether it is reasonable.
The reasonableness assessment weighs shoreline-protection interests against the owner's interests; the age of the measure, uncertainty about its legality and the cost of remedy may matter.

Structures that privatise shoreline areas and garden-like vegetation management may require strandskyddsdispens under MB 7 kap.; the court found it was not shown that these measures predated the general shoreline-protection rules introduced in 1975.

The removal order was reasonable for the fence, table and grill place, and the prohibition on garden-like vegetation management; it was unreasonable for the dock given its long presence and the earlier nearby dock.
Under MB 26 kap. 15–16 §§, the order could apply to the new owners in the ongoing case, but the unregistered fines could not be enforced against them.

evidence.contains: om verkan av att tvisteföremålet överlåts

outcome: MÖD upheld the order to remove the fence, table and grill place and to stop maintaining the area as a garden, but set aside the removal order for the dock and changed the order to apply to the new owners without any of the prescribed fines.
source: MÖD 2021:6 (M 9303-19, 2021-04-12): Tillsyn avseende strandskydd

question: I have a floating dock in a shoreline-protected coastal inlet on Tjörn, at the end of a narrow boat channel. Its inner 26 metres replaced a pre-1975 pile-supported dock after that dock was destroyed in a storm; an application in 1987 described the work as repair and replacement, and the County Administrative Board said repair of a pre-1975 dock did not require a dispensation. I later extended the floating dock by about 26 metres to reduce the need for repeated dredging. Can I keep the dock as it now stands?
key_points: Under MB 7 kap. 18 c § första stycket 1, a dispensation may be justified where the area is already taken into use in a way that makes it unimportant for shoreline-protection purposes.

A replacement dock may qualify where it is broadly comparable in size, design and location to the former dock; an application should generally be made within about one year after the former structure disappears.

The inner section was treated as a replacement because the 1987 application covered replacement and was submitted within the relevant timeframe, and the section had broadly the same size and location as the former dock.

The historical purpose of shoreline protection and the authority’s earlier advice mattered to proportionality under MB 7 kap. 25 §; the later extension was assessed separately and did not receive dispensation.

evidence.contains: redan har tagits i anspråk på ett sätt

outcome: MÖD granted shoreline-protection dispensation for the inner 26 metres but refused it for the outer extension, which had to be removed along with its anchors and chains.
source: MÖD 2021:2 (M 4972-20, 2021-01-21): Strandskyddsdispens

question: Can we place seven mooring buoys in a shoreline-protection area on the coast in Strömstad, where the water is otherwise accessible to the public? Four would be arranged along the coast about 30–50 metres apart, and three would be closer to existing piers but not used for mooring boats at those piers. The buoys would have constantly taut chains, and the area has no new mooring anchors.
key_points: MB 7 kap. 15 § 2 p. prohibits an installation or arrangement in a shoreline-protection area if it deters the public from an area where they would otherwise be free to go.
Whether buoys have a deterring effect depends on how the public can normally be expected to react, including the buoys’ size, arrangement and surroundings.
Several buoys can have a collective deterring effect because of their placement relative to one another and nearby piers, even if each buoy is considered separately.
MB 7 kap. 15 § 4 p. was not breached because the constantly taut chains did not substantially alter the living conditions of animal or plant species.
outcome: MÖD upheld the order to remove the seven buoys, finding that together they deterred the public from an area otherwise freely accessible.
source: MÖD 2020:33 (M 13094-19, 2020-11-26): Föreläggande att ta bort bojar inom strandskyddsområde

question: I am seeking a detailed development plan for a centrally located site in Halmstad that is currently used for parking, with a new building for housing, offices and commercial uses. The site is immediately next to a long-established brewery with an environmental permit, and nearby residents could be affected by noise, odours or an ammonia incident. Could plan requirements for room orientation, balconies and patios, and ventilation intakes with air treatment address these concerns?
key_points: Under PBL 2 kap. 5 and 9 §§, planning must account for the suitability of the location and prevent unacceptable risks or effects on the surroundings.

PBL 4 kap. 12 § allows a detailed plan to require protective measures; here, plan requirements concerning room orientation, balconies, patios and ventilation were considered sufficient to address risks and disturbances from the brewery.

A nearby permitted operation does not by itself prevent new housing: the court found no reason to expect the plan to restrict the brewery’s permitted activity, and complaints from future residents were not significant enough under PBL to defeat the plan.
Under PBL 4 kap. 36 §, reasonable regard must be given to existing property rights; the court considered the garage-access arrangements and 3.5-metre clearance sufficient in this case.
The plan could rely on parking outside its boundary, and the court found that the development’s parking demand could be met.

skyddsåtgärder för att motverka markförorening, olyckor, översvämning och erosion
utformad med skälig hänsyn till befintliga bebyggelse-, äganderätts- och fastighetsförhållanden

outcome: MÖD dismissed the appeals and left the adopted detailed development plan in force.

question: Can we harvest spruce on our forest land in Trosa? The planned work is within an area with three registered key biotopes and nature and cultural values of national interest; the area is also being considered for nature-reserve protection. Spruce bark-beetle damage is present, and knärot, a protected species, has been reported in the area.
key_points: Under MB 12 kap. 6 §, the supervisory authority must consider whether a reported activity could substantially alter the natural environment and may order measures to limit or prevent harm.
When assessing a consultation notification, the authority must apply the general consideration rules in MB 2 kap. and assess whether precautionary measures are needed.
The assessment must include the effect on protected species; the Species Protection Ordinance specifies the general consideration rules for species protection.

The temporary prohibition means the reported harvesting cannot proceed while the matter awaits Skogsstyrelsen’s further decision; the ruling does not finally determine whether harvesting will be allowed.

domar och beslut om tillstånd, godkännande eller dispens

outcome: MÖD rejected Skogsstyrelsen’s appeal, leaving the case remitted for further handling and the temporary prohibition on the reported harvesting in force until Skogsstyrelsen decides otherwise.
source: MÖD 2020:45 (M 13871-19, 2020-10-28): Klagorätt för miljöorganisation

question: I have a building permit in Österåker for a detached house and an additional dwelling in an ancillary building. The revised house drawings keep the same length, width and height but add an exterior door, alter some window placements and change the internal layout, including adding bathroom and utility spaces and an opening between floors. Can the house be built using these revised drawings without a new building permit?
key_points: Under PBL, only minor adjustments may be accepted within an existing building permit; more extensive revisions require a new building-permit application.
The assessment is not limited to changes in the building’s overall dimensions; changes to the façade and internal layout may also be material.
A municipal decision approving revised drawings can be appealable by affected parties under the applicable rules on appeals.
Whether the revised layout changes the building from a one-dwelling to a two-dwelling house is for the municipality to assess in a new permit review.
outcome: MÖD upheld the decision to overturn the municipality’s approval of the revised drawings, finding the changes too extensive to be covered by the existing permit and requiring a new building-permit application.
source: MÖD 2020:51 (P 6272-20, 2020-10-07): Beslut att godkänna reviderade ritningar under byggprocessen

question: Our newly built apartment building in Uppsala received a final certificate after the control plan and an accessibility expert’s report indicated that the technical requirements were met. Doors between the garage and the stairwells have door closers for fire safety but no automatic openers. Can the building committee require us to install automatic door openers if those doors are part of a communication space?
key_points: Under PBL 8 kap. 4 §, buildings must meet essential technical accessibility and usability requirements for people with reduced mobility or orientation.
Under PBL 8 kap. 5 §, the applicable technical requirements are those in force when the building was constructed.
A final certificate under PBL 10 kap. 34 § does not itself bar a later corrective order if the building fails those technical requirements.
Under PBL 11 kap. 20 §, the building committee may order the owner to correct the deficiency; whether the doors failed the applicable accessibility requirements remained for further review.

de tekniska egenskapskrav som gäller
visat att alla krav som gäller

outcome: MÖD held that a final certificate does not prevent a corrective order if the building fails the technical requirements that applied when it was built, and remitted the case to the county administrative board without finally deciding whether the order was justified.
source: MÖD 2020:52 (P 6912-19, 2020-08-27): Föreläggande om rättelse

question: I want to add a 31.5-square-metre glazed sunroom to my detached house in a residential area of Staffanstorp. The 1969 building plan treats the entire area where the sunroom would stand as dotted land that may not be built on. There are other sunrooms in the area, and the municipality has referred to about 20 permits for similar extensions.
key_points: Under PBL 9 kap. 31 b §, a building-permit application that deviates from a detailed plan can be approved only if the deviation qualifies as minor and meets the statutory conditions.
Earlier dispensations for similar construction may support treating a deviation as minor, but the evidence must establish their extent and relevance to the plan provision.
The entire 31.5-square-metre extension was on land designated as not to be built on, and the court found no other basis for considering the deviation minor.
outcome: MÖD overturned the building-permit decision and rejected the application because the deviation from the plan could not be considered minor.
source: MÖD 2020:47 (P 12265-19, 2020-08-24): Bygglov för uterum

question: I want to build an accessory building of no more than 25 m² beside my existing house in Göteborg, with a ridge height of 4 metres measured from the finished ground next to it. The site is raised about one metre above the adjacent street under a final ground permit, and the building would be less than 6 metres from the street but more than 4.5 metres from the property boundary; because of the other buildings on the site, I cannot place it at least 6 metres from the street. Would this qualify as a building-exempt project?
key_points: Under PBL 9 kap. 4 a §, a building-exempt accessory building must meet the statutory limits, including a maximum building area of 25 m², a maximum ridge height of 4.0 metres, and a minimum 4.5-metre distance from the boundary unless the neighbour consents.

PBF 1 kap. 3 § second paragraph applies when calculating the ridge height of an accessory building, even though it governs building height; within 6 metres of public space, the starting point is normally the public space’s mean level beside the site.

The PBF rule allows special reasons for using another reference level; here, the building could not be placed at least 6 metres from public space and its proposed proportions suited both the other buildings on the site and the surrounding environment.
The 4-metre ridge-height limit was met when measured from the mean ground level beside the building, so the accessory building qualified for the exemption and the startbesked was upheld.
