question: I want to build an apartment building and parking garage in the Öbacka Strand area of Umeå, where a detailed development plan applies. The apartment building would have twelve levels and two separate stairwells, with each apartment accessible from only one stairwell. The building would have two passenger lifts in total, one serving each stairwell.
key_points: PBL 8 kap. 1 § 3 and PBF 3 kap. 4 § require buildings and dwellings to be accessible and usable for people with impaired mobility or orientation.
Under Boverket’s building regulation BBR 3:144, a building with more than ten levels must provide an additional passenger lift so that all apartments have access to it.
Where stairwells are separate and apartments can access only one stairwell, each stairwell must have two passenger lifts.
A shortfall in the lift provision cannot be accepted as a minor deviation where it undermines the statutory accessibility requirement.
outcome: MÖD dismissed the appeal and upheld the refusal of building permission because the apartments did not each have access to an additional passenger lift and this could not be accepted as a minor deviation.
source: MÖD 2017:37 (P 10972-16, 2017-09-13): Ansökan om bygglov för flerbostadshus

question: We are considering a detailed plan for two four-storey apartment buildings in central Kalix, in an established neighborhood near existing homes and older protected buildings. The plan would allow about 1,000 m² of residential building area, and the municipal foundation that owns the site would build the apartments; the comprehensive plan supports densification of central Kalix. During consultation, a municipal councillor who was also vice-chair of the foundation submitted a statement supporting the plan on delegation from the municipal executive committee.
key_points: Under 6 kap. 25 § KL, a representative may be disqualified when circumstances are liable to undermine confidence in their impartiality; the councillor’s foundation role created such a conflict.

The exception in 6 kap. 27 § first paragraph KL applied because the municipality appointed at least half of the foundation’s board members and the consultation statement was not an exercise of public authority against an individual.
A consultation statement to another authority is not ordinarily an exercise of public authority unless the receiving authority is bound by it; the statement did not bind the planning authority.
The delegation prohibition in 6 kap. 34 § KL did not apply because the delegated consultation statement was not an exercise of public authority against an individual.
A detailed-plan adoption is reviewed for compliance with legal rules, with the municipality retaining its planning discretion within the applicable legal limits.
outcome: MÖD dismissed the appeal, so the decision to adopt the detailed plan was not set aside.

question: I own a home in Vintrie, Malmö, and want to build a wooden deck in the garden, about 20 cm from the property boundary and 1 m from my neighbour’s patio. The detailed plan marks this part of the property with a cross and says that only outhouses may be built there. Would the deck be allowed even if it does not require a building permit?
key_points: Under PBL 1 kap. 4 §, a building work includes a building or another structure; the court found that the wooden deck was an installation and therefore a building work.
Under PBL 10 kap. 2 § first paragraph point 2, a measure involving a building work must comply with the detailed plan even when it does not require a building permit.
The plan allowed only outhouses on the cross-marked land, and the court found no basis to interpret that restriction as allowing the deck.
Under PBL 11 kap. 5 §, the supervisory authority must examine whether to intervene when there is reason to believe a provision of the Act has not been followed.

outcome: MÖD found that the deck was a building work that contravened the detailed plan and upheld the remittal for the municipality to continue its supervision.

question: We want a detailed plan allowing a residential building of two to seven storeys on the currently open courtyard in Kungsholmen, central Stockholm, above existing shops and a garage. The building would stand parallel to an existing courtyard building, about 15.4 metres between façades, with balconies and similar features permitted to project up to 1.8 metres. A daylight study indicates that the lower apartments in the existing building, whose floors are below the courtyard level, would receive less daylight, and the new building would increase overlooking.
key_points: Under PBL 2 kap. 9 §, planning and the location, placement and design of buildings must not cause danger to health or safety or significant nuisance to the surroundings.

Whether an impact is significant nuisance is assessed in context, including the area's character and local conditions; in central Stockholm, residents must tolerate a greater degree of infill and nearby buildings.

Daylight loss and overlooking can be relevant impacts, but a daylight factor below the Boverket recommendation does not automatically constitute significant nuisance; the cited building regulations apply to new buildings and the general advice is not binding.

Assess the actual separation, relative levels, building height and permitted projections: MÖD considered the roughly 15.4-metre façade distance acceptable despite the parallel arrangement and the substantial effects on some existing apartments.

The plan clearly set out the proposed building envelope and included some adaptations to reduce impacts; the court considered the effects as a whole against the central location and expected urban changes.

outcome: MÖD dismissed the appeal and left the detailed plan in force, finding that the increased overlooking and reduced daylight did not amount to significant nuisance under PBL 2 kap. 9 §.

question: I have notified a plan to build a jetty in a water area in Tanum. The County Administrative Board did not set a different start date during the eight weeks after I filed the notification, but has since issued an interim prohibition while the notification case is still being handled. May I begin the work?
key_points: Under MB 11 kap. 9 b § third stycket, a notifiable water operation may begin after eight weeks unless the supervisory authority determines otherwise.
The authority must change the time limit within the eight-week period; after that period, it could not prohibit the operation within the notification case.
The ruling concerns the right to begin under the notification procedure and does not determine whether the project meets other applicable requirements.

outcome: MÖD quashed the County Administrative Board’s prohibition because it was issued after the eight-week period had passed without the authority changing the start date.

question: Can I obtain a five-year temporary building permit for 280 student apartments in four buildings, six to eight storeys high, in the Vällingby Parkstad area of Stockholm? The detailed plan designates the site as parkland, and the buildings would occupy only part of the green area. The modular buildings would be removable; construction would involve piles, concrete base slabs and minor adjustments to ground levels, and we plan to remove the slabs, cut the piles below ground and restore the surface with soil and grass when the permit ends.
key_points: Under PBL 9 kap. 33 a §, a temporary permit for new housing may be granted if the applicant requests it, the site can be restored and the measure meets a condition under PBL 9 kap. 30–32 a §§.

The applicant must demonstrate that the site can be restored within the permitted period; the assessment concerns the restoration of the site, including whether the proposed removal and reinstatement are practically achievable.

Restoration costs must be economically reasonable; the court accepted the assessment here because the works involved piles, base slabs and minor ground-level adjustments rather than extensive excavation, blasting or remediation.
The project must also satisfy at least one applicable condition under PBL 9 kap. 30–32 a §§; the court found no significant nuisance that would prevent the permit.
outcome: MÖD reversed the lower court and reinstated the five-year temporary building permit.
source: MÖD 2017:25 (P 11278-16, P 11330-16, 2017-06-20): Tidsbegränsat bygglov för nybyggnad av studentbostäder

question: Can we build an overdecking above the Värtabanan railway in the Albano area of Stockholm without building permission? The construction is intended to become a railway tunnel, with the area above it raised to the levels set out in the detailed development plan. It will be used for railway traffic, and the finished passage will open at both ends.
key_points: Under PBL 9 kap. 2 §, building permission is generally required for new construction of a building; the court assessed the construction’s intended completed form.
Under PBL 1 kap. 4 §, a building must be intended to be constructed so people can stay in it; this railway tunnel was not designed for that purpose.
Under PBF 6 kap. 1 § 3, tunnels intended for railway traffic are exempt from building-permit requirements.

The planned final ground level was fixed in the detailed development plan, so the structure could be assessed as a tunnel beneath the completed ground level even though it was initially built above ground.

The ruling concerned the tunnel body for railway use; tunnel entrances and later facilities for a possible passenger station may require separate permission, and the work must comply with the detailed development plan.

outcome: MÖD upheld the municipality’s decision to take no action on the complaint, finding that the construction would be a railway tunnel exempt from building permission.

question: I own a detached house in a fairly dense coastal residential area in Halmstad and want to add a roof terrace on the side facing my neighbour’s corner-lot house. The terrace would be about five metres above the neighbour’s plot and roughly five metres from the boundary, with sightlines to two windows and part of the lawn. The neighbour’s main patio facing the sea is fully screened from view, and some of the lawn and one side of the house are also screened.
key_points: Under PBL 2 kap. 9 §, significant nuisance must be substantial, and the provision is applied restrictively.
The assessment concerns the terrace’s intended use and the actual degree of overlooking into the neighbour’s home and outdoor areas.
The area’s character and circumstances on the neighbouring property matter; here, the neighbour had a fully screened patio facing the sea and other areas with limited or no overlooking.
A rooftop terrace near a neighbour is not automatically prohibited: the outcome depends on the intensity of the overlooking and the privacy available to the neighbour.
outcome: MÖD granted building permission, finding that use of the terrace did not cause a significant nuisance through overlooking in these circumstances.
source: MÖD 2017:28 (P 8828-16, 2017-06-13): Bygglov för takterrass

question: I own an existing café building at Kullaberg in Höganäs, outside a detailed development plan, and want to change it into a holiday home. The building is not next to an existing group of buildings and is close to a public bathing place and a nature area, with a public path and steps nearby. The site is within a nature reserve and Natura 2000 area, and is covered by national interests for the coast, nature, cultural environment and outdoor recreation.
key_points: Under PBL 2 kap. 2 §, land use must be appropriate in view of the site and public interests, with good management of land and water given priority.

Under MB 4 kap. 4 §, holiday homes in the protected coastal area are generally allowed only as additions to existing groups of buildings; the owners’ personal circumstances and difficulties running or selling the café were not special grounds for an exception.
Under MB 4 kap. 2 §, tourism and outdoor recreation, especially mobile outdoor recreation, must be taken into account when assessing the measure.

A change from café to private holiday home is a materially different use: the building and area around it may be perceived as private, negatively affecting public access to the bathing place and surrounding nature area.
The existing building and fencing did not make the proposed use appropriate under PBL 2 kap. 2 §, given the lasting impact on public access and the public interests at the site.

evidence.contains: mark- och vattenområden används för det eller de ändamål
turismens och friluftslivets, främst det rörliga friluftslivets, intressen särskilt beaktas
så långt möjligt skyddas mot åtgärder som kan påtagligt skada

outcome: MÖD upheld the building committee’s refusal, finding that the change to private residential use would negatively affect public access to the bathing place and surrounding nature area and was not an appropriate use of the land from the public-interest perspective.
source: MÖD 2017:32 (P 9977-16, 2017-05-10): Bygglov för ändrad användning från café till bostad

question: I own a waterfront property in Värmdö with a jetty and an accessory building in the shore-protection area. Both structures have existed since at least 1986, and I acquired the property in 2010; I had no reason to suspect that a shore-protection exemption was missing. Can I obtain an exemption to keep them?
key_points: Structures in a strandskydd area may require an exemption under MB 7 kap.; the court found these structures required one.
An exemption requires special reasons under MB 7 kap. 18 c §; the passage of time and the municipality's conduct did not provide special reasons here.

Under MB 26 kap. 12 §, an order may be directed at a new owner if reasonable; the court considered the structures' age, the owners' later acquisition, and the absence of indications of circumvention or reason to suspect the missing exemption.
The court set aside the removal orders but did not grant an exemption, so the ruling does not establish that the structures are authorised.
outcome: MÖD found no grounds for a retrospective exemption but set aside the orders requiring the new owners to remove the jetty and accessory building because removal was not reasonable in the circumstances.
source: MÖD 2017:16 (M 3186-16, M 7737-16, 2017-04-19): Vitesföreläggande om borttagande av brygga m.m.

question: I want to build a multifamily building with 41 apartments and two office premises on a vacant infill site in central Lund, joining it to an existing residential building. The area is covered by a 1929 town plan that allows buildings to be joined and sets a maximum height of 11 metres and three storeys. The existing building has large gable windows serving two of its three rooms, and the proposed adjoining building would cover those windows.
key_points: Under PBL 9 kap. 30 §, building permission within a detailed-plan area requires compliance with the plan and the applicable requirements in PBL 2 kap.
Under PBL 2 kap. 9 §, a building must not cause a significant nuisance; covering the windows to two of three rooms in an existing apartment met that threshold.

The nuisance assessment considers all circumstances, including location, use and the detailed plan; impacts already assessed and accepted through the plan are not reassessed at the building-permission stage.

The plan's permission for joined buildings did not establish that the impact of joining the proposed building to this existing house, including blocking its gable windows, had been assessed when the plan was adopted.
A building right under the plan leaves little scope to restrict the permitted development, but it does not justify a significant additional nuisance that the plan did not assess.

evidence.contains: fara för människors hälsa och säkerhet eller betydande olägenhet på annat sätt
åtgärden inte strider mot detaljplanen

outcome: MÖD overturned the building-permission decision and refused the application because covering the windows to two of three rooms in an existing apartment would cause a significant nuisance.

question: I own a plot in Smedslätten, Stockholm, within a detailed-plan area where buildings are generally required to follow the building line along the street. There is already a house on the street frontage, and I want to build an additional two-dwelling house set back behind it, with changes to the ground levels to enable construction. The plot has no unusual feature that prevents building on the prescribed line.
key_points: Under the detailed plan, buildings must follow the specified building line unless special circumstances justify a setback; that exception is to be applied restrictively.
Special circumstances must relate to a particular feature of the plot that distinguishes it from other plots in the plan area regarding the ability to comply with the building-line rule.
A desire to use the plot’s full building rights does not, by itself, establish special circumstances where those rights can be used in a plan-compliant way.
The setback was not plan-compliant, and the deviation was not minor given its nature and extent, so the building permit could not be granted.
Land works intended only to enable construction that cannot be permitted fail the requirements for a land permit under PBL 9 kap. 35 § first stycket 2 and 5a.
outcome: MÖD overturned the granted building and land permits and refused both applications because the proposed placement conflicted with the detailed plan and the land works were intended only to enable that construction.
source: MÖD 2017:12 (P 8664-16, P 8668-16, 2017-04-13): Ansökan om bygglov och marklov

question: I am considering building a single-family house on an undeveloped plot at the forest edge in Vinäs, near Lake Siljan. The site is outside any detailed plan or area regulations; part of the wider plot is within the shoreline-protection area, but the proposed house site is outside it. The open land nearby was previously used for cultivation but has not been used for crops or grazing for about 20 years, and there are homes in the surrounding area.
key_points: A preliminary ruling under PBL 9 kap. 17 § assesses whether the proposed building can be permitted at the chosen location.
Under PBL 2 kap., the authority must assess whether the land is suitable for the proposed use, including relevant land-use interests under MB 3 kap.
Under MB 3 kap. 4 §, valuable agricultural land may be used for development only when the statutory conditions are met; the evidence here did not establish that the site was such land.
The assessment of whether land is agricultural land should consider its current and recent use, condition, size, location, and effects on rational farming.
The proposed site was outside the shoreline-protection area, and no other identified planning, landscape, cultural-environment, or national-interest concern prevented the house.

evidence.contains: Brukningsvärd jordbruksmark får tas i anspråk för bebyggelse

outcome: MÖD dismissed the appeal and left the positive preliminary ruling for the house in place.
source: MÖD 2017:31 (P 6358-16, 2017-04-10): Förhandsbesked för enbostadshus

question: I am proposing a detailed plan for 23 detached houses next to the existing Sågmon holiday-home area near Katrineholm. Access would use existing private roads and connect to Route 55, where the speed limit is 100 km/h; residents would need to cross the busy road to reach the bus stop, and the proposal has no settled safe crossing or other public-transport connection. Can this plan be adopted?
key_points: Under the applicable ÄPBL 2 kap. 3 §, land must be suitable for development with regard to the possibilities of arranging traffic and other services.
Under the applicable ÄPBL 2 kap. 4 §, traffic needs, a good traffic environment and protection against traffic accidents must be considered when shaping the built environment.
A detailed plan should show that measures needed to meet the needs it generates can be carried out; unresolved traffic-safety questions can make the planned location unsuitable.

Assess safe access for pedestrians and connection to public transport as well as vehicle access; existing safety problems do not remove the need to establish a safe solution for the planned development.
outcome: MÖD annulled the decision to adopt the plan because the planning material did not show how access to the area, especially the connection to public transport, could be made safe.
source: MÖD 2017:15 (P 5959-16, 2017-03-16): Upphävande av detaljplan

question: In Österåker, I plan a hotel and holiday-cottage development across three adjacent properties: 12 cottages on one, 13 on another, and a reception/kiosk with a residential part and a guest cottage on the third. The 1953 building plan allows residential, hotel and commercial uses, but also incorporates rules requiring buildings to be at least 6 metres from the plot boundary and generally 12 metres apart, with a possible reduction to 9 metres; my proposed layout includes buildings less than 9 metres apart and one about 2 metres from a boundary.
key_points: Within a detaljplan, bygglov requires that the measure not conflict with the plan under PBL 9 kap. 30 §.
A 1953 plan’s reference to 97 §, fourth and fifth paragraphs, of the 1947 building regulations incorporated those rules as plan provisions, which remained applicable despite the regulations’ repeal.
The plan required at least 6 metres from the plot boundary and generally 12 metres between buildings; the proposed placements breached these requirements.
Under PBL 9 kap. 31 b §, deviations must be assessed together and in context; the number and extent of the deviations meant they were not minor deviations that could be accepted.
Owners of nearby properties may have a right to appeal permits when they are particularly affected by the scale and location of the proposed development.

evidence.contains: är liten och förenlig med detaljplanens syfte

outcome: MÖD found that the proposed buildings violated binding plan requirements and that the deviations were not minor, so it overturned the permits and refused all three applications.
source: MÖD 2017:13 (P 7512-16, 2017-02-27): Klagorätt i mål om bygglov

question: I own a residential property in Tranås where an old stone wall along the boundary with a neighbouring property has been replaced by a concrete retaining wall about 22 metres long and 36–80 centimetres high. A wooden structure is fixed on top of the wall. Do I need a building permit for this work, and can it proceed without one?
key_points: Under PBF 6 kap. 1 § 7 p., building permission is required to erect, move or substantially alter a wall or fence; the ruling did not decide whether permission could be granted for this wall.
Whether a structure is a wall is assessed from factors including height, length, transparency, design, location, construction, durability, purpose and effect on the surroundings.
A replacement is assessed as a newly erected wall where the former wall no longer remains; the fact that a stone wall previously stood there did not make the concrete wall permit-free.
A wooden structure fixed to and structurally joined with the wall may be treated as part of the wall rather than as a separate fence or screen.

Where a permit-required measure has been carried out without a permit, the building committee must continue supervision under PBL 11 kap.; the ruling remitted this case without deciding the permit application or its prospects.
outcome: MÖD held that the concrete wall and attached wooden structure formed a permit-requiring wall, overturned the municipality’s decision to close the supervision case, and remitted the matter for further handling.

question: Can I get a building permit outside a detailed plan in Orust’s coastal area for two joined holiday houses and a plank? The proposed buildings would sit on relatively high, open rocky ground southwest of existing houses, which are mostly grouped along the access road in lower terrain; the municipality’s comprehensive plan identifies the area to the southwest as one where building should be avoided. The coastal area is one where holiday development is restricted to additions to existing development.
key_points: In the coastal areas covered by MB 4 kap. 4 §, holiday development may come about only as additions to existing development.
An addition must not appreciably expand the area taken up by holiday development; it may instead be a natural rounding-off or densification within an existing developed area.
The proposed location on open rocky ground would expand the developed area and reduce public access to that landscape, rather than naturally rounding off the existing development.
The comprehensive plan’s guidance against building in the southwest area supported the conclusion that the proposal was an extension into an area to be avoided.
Under PBL 2 kap. 2 §, the environmental-code rules in MB 4 kap. apply when deciding a building-permit application outside a detailed plan.

evidence.contains: i form av kompletteringar till befintlig bebyggelse

outcome: MÖD revoked the building permit and refused the application because the proposed buildings were not a permitted addition to existing holiday development under MB 4 kap. 4 §.

question: I want to build three single-family homes on land south of Lake Aspen in Lerum, within the 300-metre shoreline protection area. The site is a small deciduous woodland with oak trees and other reported nature values, and the proposal would involve earthworks and tree removal. The Västra stambanan railway lies between the site and the shoreline, although a pedestrian tunnel passes beneath it.
key_points: Within the shoreline protection area, the proposed construction is prohibited under MB 7 kap. 15 § unless an exemption is granted.
A railway may make an area well separated from the shoreline and provide a special reason for exemption under MB 7 kap. 18 c § point 2; a pedestrian tunnel did not change that assessment here.
An exemption must still be compatible with the purposes of shoreline protection under MB 7 kap. 26 §.

The applicant must demonstrate that the project is compatible with those purposes; the woodland’s high nature values and the expanded protection’s aim of protecting small woodland areas meant this was not demonstrated.
The applicant’s private interest in building did not outweigh the public interest in protecting the area’s natural values.

evidence.contains: bevara goda livsvillkor för djur- och växtlivet på land

outcome: MÖD dismissed the appeal and refused strandskyddsdispens for the three houses.
source: MÖD 2016:21 (M 6995-16, 2016-12-22): Strandskyddsdispens för nybyggnad av tre enbostadshus

question: I want to extend my single-family house in Ålsten, Stockholm, and make exterior alterations. The 1929 detailed plan allows no more than two storeys and generally requires buildings over five metres high to be at least six metres from a neighbouring boundary; the existing house is about 4.5 metres from the boundary, and the proposed extension would be about 5–5.4 metres away. The drawings show a basement and planting beds along much of the façades; my calculation using the tops of those beds puts the floor above the basement 1.44 metres above the average adjacent ground level. Can I obtain building permission?
key_points: Under PBL 9 kap. 30 §, building permission within a detailed-plan area requires the proposal to comply with the plan, subject to the statutory exceptions.
Under PBL 9 kap. 31 b §, a deviation must qualify as minor; a third storey where the plan allows two could not be accepted as a minor deviation.

For the basement-storey assessment, the applicable plan rule treated the basement as a storey when the floor above it was more than 1.5 metres above the average adjacent ground level; planting beds along the façades did not determine that ground level, so the ground outside them had to be projected towards the façades.

The plan required a six-metre boundary setback for a building over five metres high; the extension’s 5–5.4-metre setback, considered together with the existing building’s deviation, was not a minor deviation.
outcome: MÖD annulled the granted building permission and refused the application because the proposal breached the plan’s storey-limit and boundary-distance requirements, and the deviations were not minor.
source: MÖD 2016:40 (P 3893-16, 2016-12-22): Bygglov för tillbyggnad samt yttre ändringar av enbostadshus

question: We have a summer cottage in Aneby municipality, in the Svartån catchment area and close to surface water. Its wastewater system is a three-chamber septic tank followed by an infiltration system, improved in 1994, and the cottage is used only during the summer. We also have a dry toilet, and connection to public sewer is not expected in the foreseeable future. Can we continue discharging toilet wastewater to the existing system, or would we need to upgrade it?
key_points: Under MB 2 kap. 3 §, precautionary measures may be required where a small sewage discharge may contribute to nutrient impacts, including through its cumulative effect with similar installations in the wider area.
A reliable catchment-level model and the area's eutrophication concerns provided sufficient support for applying a high environmental protection level in the designated area.
MB 2 kap. 7 § requires a reasonableness balance; the cost of upgrading, the seasonal use, the available dry toilet, and the lack of foreseeable public sewer connection were relevant.

The owners could not continue the existing toilet-wastewater discharge after the effective date; the prohibition was framed as a direct ban rather than a conditional requirement to prove the system's performance.
outcome: MÖD prohibited the owners from discharging toilet wastewater to the existing installation from 30 June 2017.
source: MÖD 2016:28 (M 10800-15, M 10805-15, 2016-12-14): Förbud att släppa ut toalettavloppsvatten

question: I want to replace an existing house in Enskede Gård, Stockholm, with a residential building made up of three connected building volumes, each containing two apartments, and lower the ground level as part of the construction. The 1925 city plan designates the site Ö2 and says that an open or connected building method applies. The surrounding area has detached houses and villa development.
key_points: Under PBL 9 kap. 30 §, a building permit within a detailed plan requires that the proposed measure not conflict with the plan.

For this 1925 city plan, the meaning of an open building method was interpreted with support from the 1950 Building Board guidance: buildings must be detached or joined two at a time across a common property boundary.

Three connected building volumes did not qualify as a detached building or as buildings joined two at a time across a property boundary; the deviation was neither minor nor compatible with the plan’s purpose.
The ground-level reduction was preparation for the proposed construction and had no independent significance, so the land permit was also overturned when the building permit was refused.

evidence.contains: åtgärden inte strider mot detaljplanen

outcome: MÖD overturned the building and land permits and denied the applications because the three connected building volumes did not comply with the plan’s open-or-connected building requirement, and the land-level change had no independent significance apart from the proposed construction.
source: MÖD 2016:18 (P 2238-16, 2016-11-23): Bygglov och marklov

question: I want to build a large roller coaster at the existing Kolmården zoo in Norrköping, without first preparing a detailed development plan. The site is on a coastal stretch, close to nature reserves, a Natura 2000 area, and areas of national interest for nature conservation, outdoor recreation, and cultural heritage. Traffic in the area is already strained, and the project is expected to add about 500 cars per day; it will also create noise, and red-listed species occur in and around the site.
key_points: Under PBL 4 kap. 2 § första stycket 3, detailed planning is required for a new building whose use may have a significant impact on its surroundings.

Under PBL 4 kap. 2 § andra stycket, the detailed-plan requirement can be avoided only if the relevant assessment can be made in the building-permit or preliminary-ruling process and significant environmental impact is not expected.
Assess the project’s effects together, including traffic, noise, affected property owners, the need for municipal involvement, and the sensitivity of nearby protected natural areas.

Here, the extensive traffic measures, uncertainty about noise and effects on red-listed species, and the sensitive surrounding environment meant that the project could be expected to have significant environmental impact and needed prior detailed planning.

evidence.contains: användning får betydande inverkan på omgivningen

outcome: MÖD upheld the decision to revoke the building permit, finding that the project raised issues requiring prior detailed planning.
source: MÖD 2016:24 (P 6782-15, 2016-10-27): Detaljplanekrav för uppförande av en berg- och dalbana

question: We want to build 336 modular student apartments in six buildings on leased land in an industrial area near Lundbyleden in Göteborg, for a ten-year period. The site is partly within detailed-plan areas and partly outside any detailed plan; the proposed housing does not appear to fit the existing plans. The ground is contaminated, and construction requires substantial excavation and shoring, with foundation documentation referring to piling and some blasting, although the modular buildings themselves can be dismantled. The municipality has identified other planned student-housing projects as future alternatives, while our lease runs until at least 2035.
key_points: Under PBL 9 kap. 33 §, a time-limited building permit requires that the measure satisfy at least one, but not all, of the conditions for a permanent permit under PBL 9 kap. 30–32 a §§.
Under PBL 9 kap. 33 §, the need for the measure must genuinely be temporary; concrete alternative projects may show that the need at this particular site will end.
Under PBL 9 kap. 33 §, the measure must have a real provisional character, including that it is practically and economically reasonable to remove it within the requested period.

Modular construction and the possibility of dismantling the buildings do not by themselves establish that the whole measure is temporary when substantial, costly ground and foundation works are also required.
outcome: MÖD upheld the decision to overturn the time-limited building permit because the extensive and relatively costly ground and foundation works made it impractical and economically unreasonable to remove the development within the requested period.
source: MÖD 2016:27 (P 1128-16, 2016-06-28): Tidsbegränsat bygglov

question: I want to put up a traditional fence around a sheep-grazing area on Norra Björnö in Västerås, within a shore-protection area and a nature reserve. The land was formerly open pasture but has become overgrown, and the grazing is intended to support nature conservation and preserve the area's cultural landscape. I would keep the enclosure only as large as needed and include stiles so visitors can continue to enter the area.
key_points: Under MB 7 kap. 15 §, a structure that deters the public from entering an area where they could otherwise move freely is prohibited in a shore-protection area unless an applicable exception or dispensation applies.
Under MB 7 kap. 18 c § first paragraph 5, an important public interest may be a special reason for dispensation when it cannot be met outside the shore-protection area.
Nature-conservation and cultural-environment purposes can support dispensation when the measure provides long-term public benefits and needs to be located in the protected area.
The enclosure's size was adapted to the shore-protection constraints, and its stiles were positioned to make public access easier; those design features supported dispensation.
The agricultural or forestry exception did not apply because the evidence did not show that the municipality or tenant was carrying on forestry or agriculture as a business.

evidence.contains: avhåller allmänheten från att beträda ett område
behöver tas i anspråk för att tillgodose

outcome: MÖD granted strandskyddsdispens for the fence and set aside the order to remove it and restore the land.
source: MÖD 2016:10 (M 11556-15, 2016-06-27): Strandskyddsdispens

question: We operate a restaurant, café and conference venue on leased land at Norra Björnö in Västerås, within Björnön nature reserve. We want to place a kåta for the venue’s activities, but the leased area is entirely within the shoreline-protection zone; there is also ground near Björngården that is already used. Can we obtain a strandskyddsdispens for the kåta at our proposed location?
key_points: Under MB 7 kap. 18 c § first paragraph, the listed special grounds for a strandskyddsdispens are exhaustive.

For expansion of an ongoing business under MB 7 kap. 18 c § first paragraph 4, the applicant must show that the expansion cannot be carried out outside the area covered by the application; the fact that the entire leased area is shoreline-protected is not enough.
The applicant must support the need for the proposed location; the possibility of placing the building on already-used land is relevant to whether the required special ground exists.
The public interest in preserving shoreline access and the purposes of shoreline protection can outweigh the private interest in using the proposed site.

evidence.contains: behövs för att utvidga en pågående verksamhet och utvidgningen inte kan genomföras utanför området

outcome: MÖD refused the strandskyddsdispens because the municipality had not shown that the kåta could not be placed on already-used land, but overturned the removal order because the municipality did not control the building.
source: MÖD 2016:11 (M 11547-15, 2016-06-27): Strandskyddsdispens

question: I want to replace the outer floating section of an existing dock in Gårvik, Orust, changing it from wood to concrete. Nearby property owners dispute whether the dock and its associated use of the water area affect water areas they own or have rights to.
key_points: An installation or alteration in a water area is water activity under MB 11 kap. 3 §, and the general rule is that water activity requires a permit under MB 11 kap. 9 §.

Notification can replace a permit only for specified smaller water activities; the authority may require a permit assessment under the Water Activities Ordinance when private interests may be affected.
The operator must have rådighet over the water area under 2 kap. 1 § lagen med särskilda bestämmelser om vattenverksamhet, for both permitted and notified activities.

A non-obviously unfounded objection about rådighet, where the relevant property rights are unclear and disputed, means the activity cannot be assessed through notification and should instead undergo permit review.
outcome: MÖD upheld the prohibition on carrying out the dock replacement under the notification procedure, finding that a permit assessment was required because the objection that the association lacked the right to use the water area was not clearly unfounded.
source: MÖD 2016:41 (M 9061-15, 2016-06-08): Anmälan om vattenverksamhet

question: I want to add a roughly 27.5-square-metre terrace at the ridge of my detached house in a coastal village in Halmstad, reached by an outdoor staircase. The terrace would be on the side nearest a neighbouring home, about 16 metres away; the neighbouring property is higher and the terrace would overlook its garden and house. The area consists of relatively closely spaced detached villas beside the sea, and the building department considers the proposal consistent with the detailed plan.
key_points: Under PBL 2 kap. 9 §, a building or its intended use must not cause significant nuisance to the surrounding area.
Assess significant nuisance in light of the character of the area and the conditions there, including what residents could reasonably expect in that setting.
Consider the intended use of the structure, not only its physical construction; terrace use that creates a pronounced sense of being overlooked can be decisive.
A relatively short distance and views into neighbours’ outdoor areas and home can amount to significant nuisance even where the proposal is considered consistent with the detailed plan.
outcome: MÖD overturned the building-permit approval and refused the application, finding that use of the terrace would cause significant nuisance through overlooking in light of the area’s character and what could reasonably be expected there.
source: MÖD 2016:37 (P 7798-15, 2016-04-26): Bygglov för takterrass

question: I own a home containing one dwelling in a row of four attached homes in Åre, within a detailed-plan area. Each home is on its own property, has its own entrance from the adjoining ground, and has its own adjoining plot, which is more than just a patio. I want to add 15 m² to the gable; the proposed extension’s distance from the boundary and height relative to the roof ridge have not been specified here.
key_points: Under PBL 9 kap. 4 b §, a building-permit-exempt extension to a one- or two-dwelling house may be no larger than 15 m², must not exceed the house’s ridge height, and must be at least 4.5 m from the boundary unless affected neighbours consent.
Under PBL 9 kap. 4 b §, attached row houses, semi-detached houses and linked houses can qualify; attachment to other homes does not by itself make the dwelling part of a multi-dwelling building.

To distinguish a qualifying one- or two-dwelling house from a multi-dwelling building, assess whether the claimed unit is a self-contained part containing no more than two dwellings; its own entrance from adjoining ground can support that view.
The dwelling must have its own plot directly adjoining it, and that plot must be more than just a patio; property boundaries, prior permits and tenure form are not decisive.

A notification is required under PBF 6 kap. 5 §, and work requiring notification may not start before the building committee issues a startbesked under PBL 10 kap. 3 §; the ruling did not decide whether the other startbesked requirements were met.

evidence.contains: påbörjas innan byggnadsnämnden har gett ett startbesked

outcome: MÖD dismissed the municipality’s appeal, finding that attached one- or two-dwelling houses can qualify for the Attefall extension exemption, and left the municipality to assess the remaining requirements for a startbesked.
source: MÖD 2016:25 (P 4803-15, 2016-04-18): Anmälan avseende tillbyggnad

question: I own a home in a planned area in Hässleholm, in a row of six attached homes, each on its own property with property boundaries along the dividing walls. My home has its own entrance and adjacent yard, and the homes are visually set back from one another; the detailed plan marks some surrounding land as non-buildable. Can I notify the municipality that I intend to build a carport as an Attefall complementary building beside my home?
key_points: Under PBL 9 kap. 4 a §, Attefall measures may apply beside an attached one- or two-dwelling house; attached homes are not automatically excluded because they form a row.
The assessment focuses on whether the claimed home is a distinct unit with no more than two dwellings; its own entrance from adjoining ground supports that assessment.
The home must also have its own plot directly adjoining it, with more than just a patio; property boundaries, plot division, and tenure form are not decisive by themselves.
PBL 9 kap. 4 a § sets further conditions, including a maximum 25 m² building area, a maximum 4 m ridge height, and restrictions on distance to boundaries and railway tracks.

A qualifying measure still requires a notification under PBF 6 kap. 5 § and may not begin before a startbesked under PBL 10 kap. 3 §; the ruling did not finally decide every requirement for this carport.

evidence.contains: av ett en- eller tvåbostadshus
påbörjas innan byggnadsnämnden har gett ett startbesked

outcome: MÖD dismissed the municipality’s appeal, holding that the home could qualify as a one-dwelling house under the Attefall rules, and left the notification for further handling.
source: MÖD 2016:26 (P 7340-15, 2016-04-18): Anmälan avseende komplementbyggnad

question: I want to build a single-family house in Öckerö in an area covered by a building plan that allows at most one storey. The proposed house has a traditional gable roof, and its section drawing gives the difference between the calculated building height and the top of the attic floor as 0.6 metres, although a scale measurement of the drawing could suggest a greater figure. The house would also exceed the plan’s stated building-area limit and extend about 4 square metres onto marked no-build land; a neighbouring house is nearby.
key_points: Under ÄPBF 9 §, an attic counts as a storey only if the calculated building height is more than 0.7 metres above the top of the attic floor.
A dimension stated on a drawing takes precedence over a scale measurement of that same drawing; scale measurement may be used when no dimension is given and the drawing is to scale.
Under PBL 9 kap. 30 §, a permit for a measure within a detaljplan generally requires that the measure not conflict with the plan.
Under PBL 9 kap. 31 b §, a small deviation may be permitted if it is consistent with the purpose of the detaljplan.
The court also found that the building’s placement, area and effects on the neighbour did not prevent the permit in this case.

evidence.contains: åtgärden inte strider mot detaljplanen
är liten och förenlig med detaljplanens syfte

outcome: MÖD held that the attic did not count as a storey because the dimensioned drawing specified a 0.6-metre difference, and reinstated the building permit.
source: MÖD 2016:6 (P 5768-15, 2016-04-14): Bygglov för nybyggnation av enbostadshus

question: Can we adopt a detailed plan for 600–700 homes, buildings up to eleven storeys, and local streets in Arenastaden near Råstasjön in Solna? About half of the 11.7-hectare plan area is within 100 metres of the lake, and the area includes woodland, scrub, open land and gravelled areas used for storage or other activities. Temporary construction huts are also present under time-limited shoreline-protection exemptions, and the proposal would lift shoreline protection for the housing blocks and streets.
key_points: Under MB 7 kap. 18 c § first stycket 1, land counts as already taken into use only where it has been lawfully appropriated in a way that makes it insignificant for shoreline-protection purposes.
Temporary shoreline-protection exemptions for construction huts do not, by themselves, establish that the land is permanently taken into use.
Under MB 7 kap. 18 c § first stycket 5, an urgent public interest supports lifting protection only if it cannot be met outside the protected area; the alternatives must be examined.
Under PBL 4 kap. 17 §, a detailed plan may lift shoreline protection only where special grounds exist and the interest in using the land outweighs shoreline-protection interests.

question: I want to build a single-family house with accessory buildings in the Vika area of Falun, on land designated as an LIS area in the municipality’s comprehensive plan. The proposed house would be about 25 metres from an existing dwelling; the proposed plot boundary would be about 25 metres from Lake Runn’s shore, with a small gravel road between the plot and the shore. The building site is agricultural land, and the plan’s LIS-area description is relatively general.
key_points: Under MB 7 kap. 18 e §, an LIS area must be suitable for rural development and limited in a way that still protects shoreline purposes in the long term; the comprehensive plan guides but does not decide this assessment.
Under MB 7 kap. 18 d §, an exemption for a single-family house in an LIS area may rely on the house being located adjacent to an existing dwelling; here the house was about 25 metres from one.
A municipality’s LIS designation is not conclusive, particularly if the County Administrative Board has objected; the court must assess the evidence and reasons for the specific area.
The court considered the area’s relationship to Vika and the municipality’s account of local services and development, as well as the limited effect of the proposal on shoreline purposes.

The proposal was on agricultural land, but the court found that the location and circumstances—including the road between the plot and shore—would not harm plant and animal life or undermine the long-term purposes of shore protection.

question: I operate a bed-and-breakfast and hostel in Kungsbacka and want to use the same building and area to provide furnished, temporary accommodation for asylum seekers, with reception and cleaning services. Stays may be longer than an ordinary hostel visit while residents await decisions on their asylum applications; do I need building permission for the change?
key_points: Under PBL 9 kap. 2 § första stycket 3 a, a change of use requires building permission only if the building is taken into use for a substantially different purpose.
Asylum accommodation intended as temporary lodging is most comparable to a hotel, hostel or campsite.
The fact that residents may stay longer because they lack other accommodation does not by itself change the character of the use.
A different conclusion may follow if the operation is adapted so that it is equivalent to ordinary housing.
Even when permission is not required, technical building requirements still apply, and a change that substantially affects fire safety may require notification.

question: I own a residential plot in Orust next to a neighbour’s plot, with a stone wall along the boundary. The existing house dates from the 1950s, and some filling was done before the area’s detailed plan was adopted in 1969; I have now raised parts of the plot by about 40–50 cm. The raised ground creates a substantial level difference with the neighbour’s plot. Do I need a marklov for this work?
key_points: Under the applicable ÄPBL 8 kap. 9 §, a substantial change in the level of land within a plot requires marklov unless the detailed plan provides otherwise.
A change of around 50 cm may be a guideline for what counts as substantial, but it is not an automatic threshold.
Assess the change in light of the conditions at the site, including the surrounding land, the area's character, and the effects on neighbours.
Earlier filling may inform the impression and impact of later work, even if that earlier work is not itself subject to enforcement.
A finding that marklov is required does not determine whether a permit would be granted.
outcome: MÖD found that the 40–50 cm raising was a substantial change in level requiring marklov and upheld the decision to return the matter to the municipality for continued supervision.

question: I want to build a multifamily building in central Lund on a site covered by a detailed development plan that allows the proposed building, which would use almost all of the permitted development rights. The site is beside an existing residential building, and the buildings would meet at a narrow angle; the proposed courtyard-facing access galleries would be about two metres from some neighbouring windows. Can I obtain building permission for this design?
key_points: Under PBL 2 kap. 9 §, a building’s placement and design must not cause a significant nuisance to its surroundings.

When assessing nuisance under PBL 2 kap. 9 §, consider all circumstances, including the location, use and detailed plan; effects already assessed and accepted through the plan are not reconsidered in the building-permission case.
The proposed building largely used the detailed plan’s building rights, and the narrow angle meant neighbours would experience substantial overlooking regardless of the new building’s design.
The overlooking from the access galleries was an additional significant nuisance, even in a central urban setting where some overlooking must be tolerated.
Where an alternative design, such as screening along the galleries, could reduce the nuisance without restricting the plan’s building rights, permission for the submitted design should be refused.

outcome: MÖD overturned the building permission and refused the application because the access galleries would cause significant overlooking that the neighbours should not reasonably have to tolerate.

question: I want to build three detached homes on land in Upplands-Bro that is outside a detailed development plan and area regulations. The building-permit drawings show multiple doorways but do not state their clear passage widths; the drawings are to scale and most other dimensions are specified.
key_points: Outside a detailed development plan, a building permit under PBL 9 kap. 31 § requires the measure to meet the applicable requirements in PBL 8 kap.
PBL 8 kap. 1 § requires a building to be accessible and usable for people with reduced mobility or orientation ability; this design requirement must be assessed at the building-permit stage.
Under PBL 9 kap. 21 §, the application must include the drawings and other information needed for the assessment.
When door widths are not dimensioned, the scaled drawings may be used to assess the door passages; an intention to meet the requirements later is not enough for a permit.
The applicant may be able to obtain a permit after supplementing the application with drawings showing compliant door-passage widths.

question: I have an open timber framework with beams and slatted sides attached to one end of my house in Lerum, close to the neighbouring property boundary. The roof covering has been removed, but the beams remain, and the property is within a detailed-plan area. My neighbours object to the structure; can I keep it?
key_points: Under PBL 1 kap. 4 §, an extension increases a building’s volume; in this case the remaining framework without roof covering was not an extension requiring building permission.
Under PBL 1 kap. 4 §, a building work includes a building or other installation, so the framework could still be assessed under PBL even though it did not require building permission.
Under PBL 10 kap. 2 §, a measure that does not require permission must comply with the applicable detailed plan or area regulations, subject to the statutory exceptions.

Under PBL 2 kap. 9 §, the location, placement and design of a building work must not cause significant nuisance; the municipality had not assessed plan compliance or nuisance, so the case was remitted.

outcome: MÖD upheld the remittal, finding that the structure without roof covering was not an extension requiring building permission but was a building work that must be assessed for compliance with the detailed plan and whether it causes significant nuisance.

question: I want to build a 46.5 m² garage and storage building 1.5 metres from my neighbour’s boundary in a residential area of Katrineholm. The area is covered by a 1968 town plan for detached housing, which has no boundary-distance rule; much of my 865 m² lot is marked as land that may not be built on, and access points on two road boundaries are restricted. My house is near the neighbour’s boundary, and moving the garage farther into the lot may obstruct visibility when entering or leaving it. The neighbour’s house is about 11 metres from the proposed garage.
key_points: Under 39 § byggnadsstadgan, which applied as a provision in the older detailed plan, a building generally had to be at least 4.5 metres from the neighbouring boundary, subject to an exception.
Special reasons for an exception can exist where no other suitable location is reasonably available on the property; the project should also meet an important need for that property.
The exception requires that the closer placement cause no disadvantage to the neighbour and present no relevant health, fire-safety, or traffic-safety hazard.
If the exception does not apply, a departure from the plan must independently meet the requirements for a minor deviation under PBL 9 kap. 31 b §.
outcome: MÖD found that the property had no reasonable alternative garage location and that the building could be placed without disadvantage to the neighbour, so it reinstated the building permit.

question: I want to build a 39 m² garage and a 25.2 m² carport on my 954 m² property in Ludvika, connected to my existing 84.4 m² house by a roughly 13 m² structure of beams and widely spaced slats. The 1941 detailed plan allows one main building and one outbuilding, limits the outbuilding to one-third of the main building's area, and limits the total building area on the plot to one-fifth of the plot. Can I obtain building permission for this project?
key_points: Under PBL 1 kap. 4 §, a tillbyggnad requires a change that increases a building's volume; a structure that does not qualify as a roof may not connect a separate building to the house as an extension.
The relevant roof test was whether the structure provided protection from the external climate; widely spaced slats forming a pergola did not meet that test.
Under the detailed plan, an outbuilding could occupy no more than one-third of the main building's area; the garage and carport exceeded that limit when treated as a separate accessory building.
Under PBL 9 kap. 31 b §, a deviation may be accepted only if it is minor and compatible with the plan's purpose; MÖD found the excess too large to qualify.

outcome: MÖD overturned the building permit, finding that the slatted pergola was not a roof and the garage and carport therefore formed an accessory building that exceeded the plan's limit and could not be treated as a minor deviation.

question: I want to densify the residential area at Gummarpsnäset on the northern shore of Lake Mycklaflon, where there are already holiday homes, and the municipality’s comprehensive plan identifies the area as suitable for rural development in shore-adjacent locations. The plan would allow additional housing and lift shoreline protection in parts of the area. The service towns the municipality identifies are several kilometres away, including Hult about 13 km and Bellö about 7.6 km by road, while a camping site is about 2.5 km away.
key_points: A municipality may lift shoreline protection in a detailed plan under PBL 4 kap. 17 § only where special grounds exist and the development interest outweighs shoreline-protection interests.
Under MB 7 kap. 18 d §, a shoreline location may be a special ground in a LIS area if the measure contributes to rural development.
A municipal comprehensive plan’s LIS designation is guidance, not binding; the site must meet the LIS criteria in MB 7 kap. 18 e §.

Where the claimed benefit is support for services in nearby towns, the distance to those towns and evidence of a likely service benefit matter; here the distances were substantial and no supporting evidence was presented.
If lifting shoreline protection is necessary to implement the detailed plan and there are no special grounds, the plan must be annulled.

outcome: MÖD annulled the detailed plan, finding that the area did not qualify as a LIS area, that no other special grounds justified lifting shoreline protection, and that the plan could not be implemented without that lifting.

question: I own a residential property in Kungsbacka next to a large forestry property, and I want to transfer 351 square metres from it to my property. The land to be transferred is outside the detailed-plan area, although my existing property is inside it, and the area has been used as part of my yard. The detailed plan has no property-division provisions, and the comprehensive plan does not identify the forestry land as a future development area. Can the property regulation be approved?
key_points: Under FBL 3 kap. 2 §, property formation must not conflict with the detailed plan, but a property crossing the plan boundary is not automatically prohibited.
Under FBL 3 kap. 3 §, property formation outside a detailed plan must not hinder appropriate land use, cause unsuitable development, or obstruct suitable future planning.
A planning authority’s objection is important under FBL 3 kap. 3 §, but it must state concrete grounds that can be examined; general concerns about possible development are insufficient.
The absence of property-division provisions and evidence that the plan boundary was intended to define the residential property supported allowing the property to cross that boundary.

outcome: MÖD reversed the lower court and reinstated Lantmäteriet’s decision approving the property regulation.

question: I own a holiday house in a coastal area in Gotland municipality and want to extend it northward. The shoreline is nearby, and although I believe the extension is more than 100 metres from it, the distance is disputed; the land is uneven. A 1978 decision marks the existing plot boundary, and the planned extension would mostly lie beyond that boundary, with another holiday house nearby. Can I obtain a shoreline-protection exemption for the extension?
key_points: Under MB 7 kap. 14 §, shoreline protection normally extends 100 metres horizontally from the shoreline at normal mean water level; a measurement from a marked shoreline on Lantmäteriet map material will normally be sufficiently accurate.
Under MB 7 kap. 15 § 2, an extension is prohibited if it deters or prevents public access; assess both the building itself and the land that would be taken into use around it.

A tomtplatsavgränsning indicates what land is considered already taken into use; land outside it is not treated as taken into use merely because the owner claims it as private or a neighbouring property has a home-frid zone.

A dispensation requires special grounds listed in MB 7 kap. 18 c §; where an extension increases privatisation of currently accessible land, that land cannot ordinarily be considered already taken into use.
MB 7 kap. 25 § requires consideration of individual interests but does not allow a dispensation on grounds beyond those specified in MB 7 kap. 18 c–d §§.

hindrar eller avhåller allmänheten från att beträda ett område
vad som krävs för att

outcome: MÖD dismissed the appeal, finding that the extension would take land within the shoreline protection area beyond the existing plot boundary and that no special grounds for a dispensation had been shown.

question: I want to build a detached single-family house in Gribbylund, Täby, on a 2,737 m² lot. The 1978 plan allows detached houses, limits the combined floor area to 20% of the lot, and allows two storeys up to 7.3 metres. The design includes an open carport beneath the upper floor, an open entrance area and terrace, and classical detailing; nearby houses vary in size and style, and trees screen the site toward a nature park by Lake Rönninge.
key_points: For building permission within a detailed plan, the measure must comply with the plan under PBL 9 kap. 30 §; here the plan allowed floor area of up to 20% of the 2,737 m² lot, or 547.4 m².

The plan regulated floor area, not open area; under the applicable area-measurement standard, the open carport, entrance area and terrace were excluded from the floor-area calculation, so they did not make the building exceed the plan’s limit.

Because the plan did not regulate the permitted extent of open area, its volume had to be assessed under the adaptation requirements in PBL 2 kap. 6 §, rather than treated as an excess of the plan’s floor-area allowance.

PBL 2 kap. 6 § requires suitable placement and design considering the townscape, site values and overall effect; the lot’s size, location, screening trees and varied surrounding buildings supported the proposed volume and placement.
PBL 8 kap. 1 § 2 requires good form, colour and material effect; a distinctive architectural style can satisfy the adaptation requirements even when it differs from nearby buildings.

outcome: MÖD reversed the lower court and upheld the building permit, finding the house plan-compliant and suitably adapted to its surroundings.

question: I own a residential property in Partille and want to secure an easement for an existing water and sewer service line that crosses a neighboring residential property. The properties are covered by a detailed plan and property plan; the detailed plan allows building only within a narrow area on the neighboring, currently undeveloped lot. The property plan shows an area for underground utilities elsewhere in the block but no easement across these properties, and the neighboring property connects by a strip of land to a municipal street. An alternative route has been proposed, but the parties disagree about its feasibility and cost. Can the easement be established along the existing route?
key_points: Under FBL 3 kap. 2 §, property formation within a detailed-plan area must not conflict with the plan; the assessment includes applicable property-plan provisions.
A plan’s failure to specify a particular easement does not automatically bar it, but its purpose and other provisions must be considered, with particular care when the plan is a property plan.
An easement that further restricts the buildable area may conflict with the plan’s intended property layout and cannot be treated as a minor deviation where it undermines the plan’s purpose.
Under FBL 5 kap. 8 §, property regulation must not make the burdened property less suitable for its intended use.
Under FBL 5 kap. 6 §, the proceeding is confined to the measure requested; alternative routes need not be assessed when the applicant maintains a claim limited to the existing route.

i mindre mån än före

outcome: MÖD upheld the decision to stop the property-formation proceeding, finding that the requested easement conflicted with the detailed plan and would make the neighboring property less suitable for its intended use.

question: I want to build three wind turbines in an area near Lilla Edet. The comprehensive plan identifies the area as important for recreation and a largely unaffected area, and says wind turbines should be avoided there; the area had also previously been designated of national interest for wind power. The Bohusleden trail is about 400 metres from the proposed turbines, and existing turbines are about 1.5 kilometres away.
key_points: Under MB 3 kap. 8 §, designation as an area of national interest for wind power does not automatically require approval of a particular project.
A current, well-supported översiktsplan is important in assessing a suitable location for wind turbines, although it is not binding.
The plan’s support for recreation and outdoor life must be weighed against the wind-power interest and the project’s effects on the site.
Here, the area’s importance as a nearby recreational and largely unaffected area, including the trail about 400 metres away, supported the conclusion that it was unsuitable for the proposed turbines.
outcome: MÖD dismissed the company’s appeal, so building permission was not granted for the three turbines.

question: I want to convert a former staff building at a site in Torsby where a forestry industry operated for many years into a holiday home. Several other small work-related buildings stand nearby, and part of the yard is gravelled; the site is close to the water, with a steep slope separating it from the area nearest the shore. A neighbouring home is nearby, but the other buildings have been used for the former business rather than as homes. Can I obtain a strandskyddsdispens for the change of use?
key_points: Under MB 7 kap. 15 § 2, changing a building’s use is prohibited if it deters or prevents public access; converting the staff building to a holiday home would extend the private sphere and require a dispensation.

The special ground in MB 7 kap. 18 c § 1 requires that the area already be taken into use in a way that makes it irrelevant to the purposes of shoreline protection; buildings without their own home-privacy zones and a partly gravelled yard did not meet that test.
An increase in privatisation, and consequent reduction of land accessible under the right of public access, means the area cannot be treated as already taken into use before the proposed change.
MB 7 kap. 25 § requires consideration of individual interests but does not allow dispensation on grounds other than those specified in MB 7 kap. 18 c–d §§.
Under MB 7 kap. 26 §, a dispensation must be compatible with the purposes of shoreline protection; no applicable special ground was established here.

question: Our boating association wants to acquire by fastighetsreglering a water area in Kyrkesund from the municipality, where our existing small-boat harbour is located. The municipal property is large and serves several purposes, and the area in question is designated in the detailed plan as water area and water area with piers. This is the only part of the municipal property that allows use as a small-boat harbour.
key_points: Under 5 kap. 8 § FBL, compare each affected property’s suitability before and after the regulation; a property must not become less suitable for its intended purpose.
A property may have several purposes, and the municipality’s long-standing permission for the association to use the area does not remove the harbour purpose from the property.
The transfer would remove the only area enabling a small-boat harbour, so the municipal property would become less suitable for that purpose.
The court found no obstacle under the general suitability requirement in 3 kap. 1 § FBL, but that did not overcome the separate restriction in 5 kap. 8 §.

question: I want to add an 8.5 m², single-storey extension with a balcony to my house in Karlskrona, more than 4.5 metres from the property boundary. The entire extension would sit on land marked in the detailed plan as not to be built on; the plan description also calls for a coherent architectural character in the area. The extension would have the same size and design as some other extensions in the area. Can I obtain a building permit?
key_points: A building-permit application must be assessed under the building-permit rules even if the measure has become exempt from the permit requirement; the applicant may instead withdraw the application.
Under PBL 9 kap. 31 b §, a deviation in a detailed-plan area must be minor and consistent with the plan’s purpose to be accepted on that basis.
Assess whether a deviation is minor in the circumstances of the individual case, including its potential precedent-setting effect and the plan’s intended character for the area.
An 8.5 m² extension placed entirely on land where building is prohibited, with potential precedent effects and a conflict with the planned architectural character, was not an acceptable deviation.

evidence.contains: är liten och förenlig med detaljplanens syfte

outcome: MÖD refused building permission because the extension’s deviation from the detailed plan was not minor and consistent with its purpose.

question: I want to build a 12-storey building with about 60 apartments for older residents in Hyllie, next to Södertorpsgården’s existing activities. The proposed southern location is parkland, while a northern alternative would use already paved land. Malmö’s planning material identifies the area for housing and services as well as parkland; can the project proceed?
key_points: Under 6 kap. 25 § kommunallagen, a municipal representative is disqualified where a particular circumstance is apt to undermine confidence in their impartiality; the member’s board role in the association connected to the planned housing met that test.
Under 6 kap. 24 § kommunallagen, a disqualified member may not participate in or attend handling of the matter; participation in plan handling can include preparatory stages.

Under 6 kap. 26 § kommunallagen, disqualification may be disregarded only when the impartiality issue obviously has no significance; that exception did not apply because the member participated when the preferred location was chosen.
The ruling set aside the plan adoption on procedural grounds and did not determine whether the housing project was substantively suitable or could be approved through a properly conducted process.
outcome: MÖD quashed the detailed-plan adoption because a committee member was disqualified and it was not obvious that the impartiality issue had no significance.
source: MÖD 2015:4 (P 9209-14, 2015-02-03): Jäv enligt 6 kap. 25 § kommunallagen

question: I have a seasonal cabin in Linköping municipality, more than a kilometre from Svinstadsjön, with summer-only water and no toilet. Dishwater and other bath, dish and laundry water go to a stone pit; its age, design and placement are undocumented, and I use the water for garden irrigation. Can I continue using this arrangement during the summer?
key_points: Under MB 9 kap. 2 §, bath, dish and laundry water is wastewater, and its discharge is environmentally hazardous activity.
Under MB 9 kap. 7 §, wastewater must be treated or otherwise handled so that no nuisance to human health or the environment arises.
The person discharging wastewater bears the burden of showing that the installation meets the Environmental Code’s treatment requirements; the undocumented stone pit did not do so.
Under MB 26 kap. 9 §, a prohibition must not be more intrusive than necessary, but MÖD found this prohibition justified.

evidence.contains: avledas och renas eller tas om hand
Mer ingripande åtgärder än vad som behövs i det enskilda fallet

outcome: MÖD upheld the prohibition on discharging wastewater to the stone pit, with the prohibition taking effect on 1 July 2015.
source: MÖD 2015:1 (M 7529-14, 2015-02-02): Förbud mot utsläpp av orenat avloppsvatten

question: I own a residential property in the Eskön area of Gävle, with two homes and outbuildings, and would like to add about 400 square metres of adjoining forest land to it. The area has long been used to store and handle firewood for the homes, and the ground on the rest of my property makes it unsuitable for that use. The forest property is owned by a developer whose adopted detailed plan provides for ten homes nearby, and the developer says a route across the area is important for residents to reach the sea. Can the land be transferred to my property against the owner's objection?
key_points: Under FBL 5 kap. 5 §, a requested fastighetsreglering may be allowed only if it improves the applicant's property; proximity to existing homes and a useful buffer area supported improvement here.
Under FBL 5 kap. 4 §, the measure must produce a more suitable property division or more appropriate land use, with benefits outweighing costs and disadvantages.
The court assessed the alleged effect on planned housing values and access to the sea against the evidence, including whether the route could be placed outside the transfer area.
Under FBL 5 kap. 7 §, land with a building may be transferred where the building has only negligible value and the transfer causes no substantial inconvenience to an interested party.

evidence.contains: lämpligare fastighetsindelning eller eljest mer ändamålsenlig markanvändning vinnes

outcome: MÖD dismissed the appeal and upheld the transfer, finding that the receiving property would be improved, the land use made more appropriate, and the benefits greater than the costs and disadvantages; the building on the area had only negligible value.
source: MÖD 2014:53 (F 238-14, 2014-12-11): Fastighetsreglering

question: Can shares in a jointly owned shoreline area in Tjörn be transferred to my farm property and a nearby holiday-home property to support use of the shore and boat moorings? The area has a pier and a boathouse, lies partly within land designated as public park in the detailed development plan, and the existing co-owners’ shares would not change.
key_points: Under FBL 6 kap. 1 §, a share in a common property must serve a lasting need of the receiving property; the court found the requested transfers did not satisfy the requirements.

FBL 6 kap. 5 § means co-owners whose share ratios do not change need not join the agreement, but they may still be parties to the proceeding and the measure is not automatically permitted against their wishes.
An ideal share in common land does not necessarily give a property a right to a boat place; the court identified an agreement or, if possible, other cadastral measures as alternatives.

The common shoreline area was partly designated as public park in the detailed development plan, and MÖD agreed with the lower court’s assessment of the possibility of allocating such land to the requested purposes.
outcome: MÖD upheld the decision to discontinue the land-regulation proceeding, finding that the requested transfers should not proceed and that the properties’ need for a lasting boat-place right should be addressed by another means.
source: MÖD 2014:50 (F 2985-14, 2014-12-08): Fastighetsreglering avseende överföring av andelar i samfällighet

question: I have a building permit for a single-family house and garage in Höganäs, and construction is underway. An inspection report has identified substantial construction defects and microbial growth, and raises concerns about whether the roof structure can withstand strong winds. Can I continue the building work?
key_points: Under the applicable older PBL 10 kap. 3 §, the building committee must prohibit work if it is obvious that the work endangers a building’s structural stability or poses a danger to human life or health.

Whether the prohibition was justified depends on the circumstances when the decision was made; the inspection report’s concerns about serious defects and the roof’s ability to withstand strong winds supported the prohibition.
Under Kommunallagen 6 kap. 36 §, a committee may authorise its chair or another designated member to decide a matter so urgent that the committee’s decision cannot be awaited.
Urgent-case authority is not restricted to particular types of matters; the relevant question is whether the decision must be made before the committee can meet.
outcome: MÖD upheld the building committee’s prohibition on continuing construction, finding that it had grounds to issue the prohibition and that the committee chair was authorised to act in the urgent matter.
source: MÖD 2014:37 (P 5474-14, 2014-11-28): Förbud mot fortsatt byggnation

question: I am involved with a public bathing place in Uddevalla that has facilities including a bathing deck, jetty and diving board. A residential house stands nearby, and we want to build a screen wall on the rocky area at the bathing place to reduce the feeling of being overlooked. The proposed wall would be 11 metres long and up to 3.25 metres high, in a place that is currently accessible to the public.
key_points: Under MB 7 kap. 15 §, an installation is prohibited if it deters the public from entering an area where they otherwise may roam freely; MÖD considered this screen wall comparable to prohibited installations and found it would restrict public access.

Under MB 7 kap. 18 c § first paragraph 1, prior use must make the area insignificant to shoreline-protection purposes; the public bathing place was not considered so taken into use that this ground applied.
Under MB 7 kap. 18 c § first paragraph 3, an installation must need to be located by the water to serve its function; the screen wall did not meet that test.
