Under MB 7 kap. 18 c § first paragraph 5, the measure must serve an important public interest that cannot be met outside the protected area; an insynsskydd for the bathing place did not qualify.

evidence.contains: hindrar eller avhåller allmänheten från att beträda
ett angeläget allmänt intresse som inte kan tillgodoses utanför området

outcome: MÖD refused the shoreline-protection exemption, finding no special grounds to allow the 11-metre screen wall.
source: MÖD 2014:45 (M 1241-14, 2014-11-27): Strandskyddsdispens

question: I want to build a 62 m² cabin where an existing 42 m² cabin stands, on a site with several other cottages and outbuildings. The site is outside a detailed development plan, about 60–100 metres from the sea and 2–3 metres above sea level, within the shoreline protection area and coastal and nature conservation interest areas. The comprehensive plan identifies this coastal landscape as sensitive, and the site is near Helsingborg and Rydebäck.
key_points: Under PBL 4 kap. 2 §, a detailed plan may be required for a new building where demand for development is high.
A larger town’s randzon may have development pressure sufficient to trigger the detailed-plan requirement, even for a limited building project.
Where strong public interests require coordinated assessment of land use and competing interests, the assessment may not be suitable for a förhandsbesked without prior detailed planning.
Under PBL 9 kap. 17 and 31 §§, the förhandsbesked assessment includes whether the measure must be preceded by detailed planning.

evidence.contains: stor efterfrågan på området för bebyggande

outcome: MÖD upheld the municipality’s refusal of a positive förhandsbesked because the area’s development should be assessed through a detailed development plan.

question: I want to build a screen around a patio and pool in a residential area of Laholm, near a road and the neighbouring property. It would be about 21 metres long and between 1.85 and 2.22 metres high, made of horizontal wooden slats with gaps, plus posts and framing. Part of it would be on land marked as no-build land in the detailed development plan.
key_points: Under PBF 6 kap. 1 § 7, erecting a plank requires building permission.
There is no statutory definition of a plank; the assessment considers height, length, transparency, overall design, purpose and impact on the surroundings.
A municipality’s local policy on fences and planks is not decisive to whether permission is required.
A construction’s transparency is only one factor; substantial height and length, and the dominant impression it makes in its setting, can make it a permit-required plank.
outcome: MÖD held that the construction was a permit-required plank and set aside the municipality’s decision to close the matter, remitting it for further handling.
source: MÖD 2014:39 (P 3438-14, 2014-11-19): Anmälan avseende olovlig åtgärd

question: I want to use occasional loads of garden soil to raise low spots, no more than about 20 cm, on agricultural land in Svedala. The soil may contain grass clumps and small roots, and I do not receive payment for accepting it. I have not made a consultation notification to the County Administrative Board.
key_points: Under 12 kap. 6 § miljöbalken, an activity that may substantially alter the natural environment must be notified for consultation; the court found that filling this agricultural land met that threshold.
A measure subject to consultation may begin no earlier than six weeks after the notification has been made, under 12 kap. 6 § miljöbalken.

Under 26 kap. 9 § miljöbalken, the supervisory authority may prohibit an activity that contravenes the Environmental Code; it need not first conduct a consultation process when the operator has failed to notify.
The prohibition was not considered excessively intrusive, and the Board’s order against further filling without its permission was upheld.

evidence.contains: komma att väsentligt ändra naturmiljön
de förelägganden och förbud som behövs

outcome: MÖD upheld the prohibition on further filling without the County Administrative Board’s permission, finding that the filling required a consultation notification and that the Board could prohibit it under 26 kap. 9 § miljöbalken without first conducting a consultation process.
source: MÖD 2014:32 (M 2184-14, 2014-10-23): Tillsynsärende; förbud mot utfyllnad av åkermark

question: I want to extend a single-family house in Stockholm to the west and south and create four apartments. The 1922 plan for the area limits buildings to 7.5 metres in height or two storeys. In the western extension, the lowest level would have living rooms, bedrooms, a bathroom and a kitchenette; its floor would be level with the ground along the west and north sides, where it would also have windows and glazed doors.
key_points: A building permit within a detailed plan must comply with the plan; the applicable plan limits buildings to 7.5 metres or two storeys.
Under PBF 9 §, a cellar counts as a storey if the floor above is more than 1.5 metres above the mean ground level, but the provision applies only if the space is a cellar.
Whether a space is a cellar requires an overall assessment of its construction and intended use; the level of the floor above relative to mean ground level is not the only consideration.

Boverket’s general advice is guidance, not binding; the lower level’s ground-level windows and doors and its intended residential use supported treating it as a storey, making the extension three storeys.
A plan deviation that exceeds the two-storey limit is not automatically acceptable as a minor deviation; MÖD found this one could not be accepted.
outcome: MÖD overturned the building permit and denied the application because the western extension would have three storeys, contrary to the plan, and this was not a minor deviation.

question: Can we obtain municipal water and sewer connections for our two neighboring properties using the connection points assigned by Värmdö municipality? One property has a permanent home, while the other is undeveloped and intended for building; both are in a detailed-plan area. The terrain is steep and rocky, one assigned point is about 65 metres from the property boundary, and the other is below a steep slope, making private service pipes difficult and costly to install.
key_points: Under 12 § of the Public Water Services Act (LAV), a connection point must meet the proximity requirement; the point assigned for one property did not.
The location must allow the property owner a practical opportunity to use the public water and sewer system; the court considered the circumstances of the site and the connection point together.
A connection point that creates exceptionally difficult or costly service-pipe works may fail the requirements even if it is near the property boundary.
A detailed plan or the municipality’s general practice does not by itself establish that a particular connection-point location meets the statutory requirements.
outcome: MÖD dismissed the municipality’s appeal and upheld the finding that the assigned connection points did not meet the requirements for enabling the owners to use the public water and sewer system.
source: MÖD 2014:23 (M 10279-13, 2014-06-13): Förbindelsepunkts läge

question: I want to build a garage with a guest cottage above it in Uddevalla, within a detailed-plan area where the maximum building height for an outbuilding is 3 metres. One corner would be about 5.5 metres from land designated as public space, although the road itself is about 8 metres away and an overgrown ditch lies between it and the property boundary. The public-space ground slopes along the boundary; can I use the ground level beside the building to calculate its height?
key_points: Under PBF 1 kap. 3 §, a building less than six metres from public space is generally measured from the public space’s average level adjoining the plot, unless special reasons justify another reference level.

The six-metre rule applies even if only part of the building is within that distance; a greater distance from the road itself and a ditch between the road and the boundary do not by themselves change the rule.
The public-space average level should generally be calculated between the boundary points from which perpendicular lines can be drawn to the building’s outer edge.
Under PBL 9 kap. 30 §, building permission within a detailed-plan area requires the measure to comply with the plan; here the applicable maximum height for an outbuilding was 3 metres.
Under PBL 9 kap. 31 b §, a plan deviation may be accepted only if it is minor and consistent with the plan’s purpose; the 0.5-metre excess in this case did not qualify.

evidence.contains: Om byggnaden ligger mindre än sex meter från allmän plats
är liten och förenlig med detaljplanens syfte

outcome: MÖD dismissed the appeal, finding that the building height exceeded the plan limit and that the deviation could not be accepted as minor.
source: MÖD 2014:17 (P 11624-14, 2014-06-04): Bygglov för nybyggnad av garage med gäststuga

question: I own a small, unplanned island in Lake Mälaren in Västerås, entirely within a strandskydd area. Two timber buildings are on the island; they were built in 1998, partly replacing an earlier building, and are intended for sheep keeping, grain storage and courses. The island is about 0.18 hectares, and sheep have not grazed there for six years; can the buildings remain without strandskyddsdispens, or would they need to be removed?
key_points: Under MB 7 kap. 15 §, new buildings are prohibited in a strandskydd area when they impede or deter public access to areas where the public may otherwise move freely.
A strandskyddsdispens under MB 7 kap. 18 c § requires special reasons and compatibility with the purposes of shoreline protection.

The agricultural exception in MB 7 kap. 16 § requires evidence that the buildings are genuinely needed for qualifying agricultural activity; the claimed activity's limited scope and uncertain duration did not establish this.

MB 26 kap. 9 § allows the supervisory authority to order measures needed to ensure compliance; MB contains no general limitation period for restoration orders, and the permanent intrusion was continuing.
The prior building did not establish a replacement-building basis because its condition, size and correspondence of purpose were not sufficiently shown.

evidence.contains: endast om det finns särskilda skäl
de förelägganden och förbud som behövs

outcome: MÖD upheld the removal order, finding that the restoration requirement was not time-barred and that the buildings did not qualify for the claimed agricultural or replacement-building exceptions.
source: MÖD 2014:27 (M 1002-14, 2014-05-07): Fråga om krav på återställningsarbete enligt miljöbalken är föremål för preskription då tio år förflutit sedan byggnad inom strandskyddat område uppförts

question: I want to enclose part of a roof terrace on my house to create a glazed room. The property is covered by a detailed plan that says part of the land may not be built on, and the terrace is mostly above a part of the house on that marked land. An earlier building permit allowed about a quarter of the house to be placed on that same restricted land.
key_points: Under 8 kap. 11 § ÄPBL, building permission within a detailed-plan area required the measure to comply with the plan, subject to the exception for minor deviations compatible with the plan’s purpose.
The detailed-plan restriction on building on marked land continued to apply even though an earlier building permit had allowed construction there.
An extension must be assessed against the plan even when it is built above ground level on an existing terrace; the location above or below ground does not remove the conflict.
Where the existing building already deviates from the plan, 8 kap. 11 § ÄPBL requires a combined assessment of the existing and proposed deviations.
Because the earlier deviation placed about a quarter of the house on restricted land, the combined deviations could not be treated as minor.
outcome: MÖD dismissed the appeal, finding that the extension and the previously accepted deviation together were too extensive to qualify as a minor deviation from the detailed plan.
source: MÖD 2014:24 (P 11603-13, 2014-05-06): Bygglov för tillbyggnad av enbostadshus

question: I want to develop about 220 apartments in buildings five to seven storeys high in the Seminariet area of Uppsala, while retaining the existing seminar buildings. The area is currently largely green and includes the seminar garden; the proposal would leave about 1.5 hectares as public park rather than the larger district park shown in the municipality’s comprehensive plan. The area is part of a national-interest cultural environment associated with Uppsala’s institutional buildings and parks.
key_points: A detailed plan that departs from the comprehensive plan triggers the applicable consultation and announcement requirements under 5 kap. 24 and 26 §§ of the former Planning and Building Act.
Under MB 3 kap. 6 §, an area of national interest for its cultural environment must be protected against measures that may cause substantial harm.
The assessment concerns the cultural environment as a whole, including the relationship between the seminar buildings, the garden and the surrounding park setting.
The municipality’s adoption of the plan could not stand where the plan both departed from the comprehensive plan and caused substantial harm to the national-interest cultural environment.

evidence.contains: skyddas mot åtgärder som kan påtagligt skada

outcome: MÖD dismissed the municipality’s appeal, leaving the decision to annul adoption of the detailed plan in place because the plan diverged from the comprehensive plan and would cause substantial harm to a national-interest cultural environment.
source: MÖD 2014:12 (P 8800-13, 2014-03-24): Antagande av detaljplan

question: I live near Västra Tommarp in Trelleborg, where a detailed plan is intended to enable further housing development. The proposal displayed for public review designated a substantial area for a local street and park with a playground as public space; the later version places that land in private development-block land for housing, with provisions for shared street, park and play facilities. Can the municipality adopt the plan in this form?
key_points: Under 5 kap. 27 § ÄPBL, a material change to a detailed-plan proposal after exhibition requires a new exhibition before adoption.
Whether a change is material depends on the purpose of exhibition, including whether it affects the plan-area environment and is of interest to the public or significantly affects affected parties.
Changing a substantial area from public street and park to development-block land can be material because the designation affects responsibility for and use of the land.
A plan adoption may be quashed for this procedural defect even though the original proposal was exhibited for the required period.
outcome: MÖD quashed the municipality’s adoption of the detailed plan because changing a substantial area from public space to development-block land was a material change requiring a new public exhibition.
source: MÖD 2014:8 (P 7464-13, 2014-03-07): Väsentlig ändring av detaljplan efter utställning

question: I am preparing a detailed plan for nine residential plots combined with horse-keeping on about 2.2 hectares in Norra Kronan, west of Vellinge. The area includes an abandoned currant orchard and is bordered mainly by farmland, with existing buildings and horse pasture nearby. It is about 1.2 km from Natura 2000 coastal meadows where the endangered green-spotted toad occurs, and there have been reports of the toad on nearby properties; the plan area has not had a site-specific environmental impact assessment.
key_points: Under the then-applicable ÄPBL 5 kap. 18 §, the environmental-assessment provisions in MB 6 kap. applied to a detailed plan that could be expected to cause significant environmental impact.
Under MB 6 kap. 11 §, a municipality must conduct an environmental assessment when a plan’s implementation can be expected to cause significant environmental impact.
The relevant assessment considers whether the plan may affect nature or areas with recognised national or international protection status, including the nearby Natura 2000 area.

A meaningful risk that the protected toad’s habitat could be damaged or destroyed supported finding likely significant environmental impact; a site visit without observations did not resolve that concern.
Where significant environmental impact is likely, an environmental impact statement must assess the effects and possible preventive or mitigating measures before the plan is adopted.
outcome: MÖD dismissed the municipality’s appeal, leaving the decision to annul the detailed plan in force because significant environmental impact could be expected and no environmental impact statement had been prepared.
source: MÖD 2014:4 (P 2823-13, 2014-01-22): Antagande av detaljplan

question: I own a house in Stenungsund and replaced an old garage with a new one without first obtaining building permission. The garage is entirely on land marked as not to be built on in the detailed plan, and its driveway is where the plan prohibits access. The plan description indicates a different garage location and access route, but the existing driveway has been used for many years and arranging the alternative route may be difficult.
key_points: Under 10 kap. 1 § ÄPBL, a measure carried out without required permission must be removed or otherwise corrected unless permission is granted afterward.
Once a final decision has established that building permission cannot be granted, the scope to avoid a correction order based on private interests is very limited.
Under 1 kap. 5 § ÄPBL, public and private interests must be weighed, but the public interest in compliance with the law and the detailed plan carries substantial weight.
The owners’ costs, the garage’s appearance, the long-standing driveway, and difficulties with the alternative route did not outweigh the public interest in demolition.
outcome: MÖD upheld the demolition order, extending the compliance deadline to 1 June 2014.
source: MÖD 2014:3 (P 4737-13, 2014-01-20): Föreläggande om rivning av olovligt uppförd garagebyggnad

question: I want to add a balcony of about 3.7 m² to an existing outbuilding in Gränna, projecting about 1.3 metres from the wall, with its underside about 2.5 metres above the ground. The building is used as a dwelling, although the detailed plan allows only outbuildings on the land where it stands. The proposed balcony would be about 1.4 metres from my neighbour’s property boundary.
key_points: Under PBL 1 kap. 4 §, an extension is a change that increases a building’s volume; the balcony’s placement and design made it a building extension.
A balcony can increase building volume even without walls when its design creates a sheltered space beneath it where people can stay.
Under PBL 9 kap. 2 §, building permission is required for an extension.
Under PBL 9 kap. 30 §, permission within a detailed-plan area requires the relevant building to comply with the plan; the dwelling-use building stood on land designated only for outbuildings.
The building’s plan conflict could not be treated as a minor deviation, so permission for the balcony could not be granted.

evidence.contains: ändring av en byggnad som innebär en ökning av byggnadens volym
den fastighet och det byggnadsverk som åtgärden avser

outcome: MÖD revoked the building permit because the balcony was a building extension and the building it was to be added to did not comply with the detailed plan.
source: MÖD 2013:41 (P 1190-13, 2013-11-12): Bygglov för uppförande av balkong

question: I want to put up an advertising sign on a narrow strip of land in Göteborg designated as public street and part of a street intended for planting. The detailed plan has no specific provisions restricting the use of this public space, and the sign would occupy only a small area in a traffic environment. A residential building is about 50 metres away; can the sign receive building permission?
key_points: Under the applicable ÄPBL 8 kap. 11 §, building permission within a detailed-plan area requires the measure to comply with the plan.
Whether an installation is compatible with an area designated as public space is assessed in light of that space’s function within the planned area.
The sign’s small footprint, its location in a traffic environment, and the very limited effect on public access supported plan compatibility.
The plan contained no specific provisions preventing this type of structure, but other requirements for permission still had to be assessed.
outcome: MÖD held that the sign was compatible with the detailed plan but remitted the case to the County Administrative Board to assess the remaining building-permit requirements.

question: Can I change a reception building built for a campground into a holiday home in Årjäng? The building is about 100 metres from the shoreline, within an area with 150 metres of shoreline protection; the campground has closed, and a nearby bathing place is used by the public. An outbuilding and a path lie between the reception building and the shore, but there is no continuous development separating the building from the shoreline; a former dwelling on the site was demolished before the reception building was built.
key_points: A shoreline-protection exemption requires a special ground under MB 7 kap. 18 c §; proportionality under MB 7 kap. 25 § cannot create grounds beyond those listed in the statute.

A site is not considered already taken into use under MB 7 kap. 18 c § merely because it was used for a campground; the reception building did not have the private character or home-privacy zone of a dwelling, and the campground had ceased operating.
An outbuilding and a path between the building and shore did not sufficiently separate the site from the shoreline to establish the relevant special ground under MB 7 kap. 18 c §.

Even if the building is about 100 metres from the shore and public access to a bathing place is maintained, an exemption must still be consistent with the purposes of shoreline protection under MB 7 kap. 26 §.

evidence.contains: tagits i anspråk på ett sätt som gör att det saknar betydelse
som krävs för att syftet med

outcome: MÖD set aside the lower court’s decision and upheld the refusal of a shoreline-protection exemption because no special grounds for an exemption had been established.
source: MÖD 2013:37 (M 5451-13, 2013-10-18): Strandskyddsdispens för ändrad användning av receptionsbyggnad

question: I want to replace an existing wind turbine on Brommö with a new, taller turbine, placed about 25–30 metres from the existing one. The proposed location is near a nature reserve with bird-protection areas and about 200 metres from a Natura 2000 area; the area is known for protected birds and bats. I have not commissioned a site-specific survey of bird and bat presence or movement patterns at the proposed location.
key_points: Under 2 kap. 1 § ÄPBL, the land-suitability assessment must balance relevant interests and apply the environmental provisions in MB chapters 3 and 4.
Under 8 kap. 20 § ÄPBL, the application must include the plans, descriptions and other information needed to decide it.
A replacement turbine may be treated as a wholly new turbine; the existence of an older operating turbine does not by itself establish that the new location is suitable.

When a proposed turbine is near protected areas and there are indications of sensitive birdlife, the application needs a sufficiently detailed, site-specific investigation; general summaries of older reports were not enough here.

evidence.contains: inte alls eller endast obetydligt är påverkade
på grund av deras naturvärden eller kulturvärden
turismens och friluftslivets, främst det rörliga friluftslivets, intressen

outcome: MÖD dismissed the appeal, leaving in place the decision that revoked the building permit because the investigation was insufficient to assess the site’s suitability.
source: MÖD 2013:33 (P 9722-12, 2013-10-09): Bygglov för utbyte av vindkraftverk

question: We are preparing a detailed plan for redeveloping Slussen in central Stockholm, replacing the existing 1930s traffic interchange with new transport infrastructure, public spaces and some commercial development. The översiktsplan identifies the area as part of a national cultural-environment interest and describes its boundaries and values, but does not set out a specific planning direction for the area. Our environmental assessment addresses the project’s impacts and alternatives, including retaining or rebuilding the existing interchange; can the plan be adopted?
key_points: Under the then-applicable PBL rules, a detailed plan deviates from an översiktsplan only when that plan establishes a relevant planning direction; identifying a national interest and describing its boundaries and values alone is not enough.
Under MB 3 kap. 6 §, areas of national cultural interest must be protected against measures that may cause påtaglig skada, but not every change to a valued area is prohibited.
An environmental assessment for a plan expected to have significant environmental effects must address its likely effects and reasonable alternatives under MB 6 kap. 11–12 §§.

Assess harm to the national interest in the context of the affected area’s overall values; the loss of the existing traffic interchange did not by itself mean the plan caused påtaglig skada to the national interest as a whole.

evidence.contains: skyddas mot åtgärder som kan påtagligt skada natur- eller kulturmiljön
kan antas medföra en betydande miljöpåverkan
skäl som ligger bakom gjorda val av olika alternativ

outcome: MÖD upheld Stockholm’s decision to adopt the Slussen detailed plan, finding that it did not deviate from the översiktsplan and could proceed without causing påtaglig skada to the national interests.
source: MÖD 2013:44 (P 11451-12, 2013-09-27): Antagande av detaljplan

question: Could a detailed plan allow additional homes in an existing residential block in central Södermalm, including homes added above existing buildings and a new building in the courtyard? The block is in a dense urban area near heavily trafficked Hornsgatan, but the courtyard is quieter and is used for recreation and children’s play. The existing 1960s buildings have been identified as having cultural-historical value, and the area also has traffic-related air-quality concerns.
key_points: Under ÄPBL 2 kap., a detailed plan must balance suitability and competing public interests, while the municipality has discretion in choosing between them.
For housing in central Stockholm, MÖD accepted the municipality’s use of the Stockholmsmodellen for traffic noise, including the importance of access to a quieter side.

Under ÄPBL 3 kap. 12 §, cultural-historical value must be considered; a cultural classification is not itself binding, and the municipality’s balancing of preservation against housing needs was accepted.

The plan’s effects on existing residents, including courtyard conditions, children’s outdoor environment and air quality, must be assessed, but the court accepted the municipality’s assessment in this case.
outcome: MÖD reversed the lower court and upheld Stockholm’s decision to adopt the detailed plan for housing in the Plankan block.
source: MÖD 2013:47 (P 11296-12, 2013-06-19): Detaljplan för bostäder

question: I want to put a small playhouse beside my home in Öckerö. It would be less than 4.5 metres from the boundary with a street, and a nearby home is about 10 metres away; a hedge stands between the playhouse and the street. Can I put it there without a building permit?
key_points: Under the ruling’s interpretation of 8 kap. 4 § ÄPBL, the 4.5-metre distance rule applies to a boundary with a street as well as to other relevant boundaries.
The neighbour-consent exception cannot be used for a boundary with a street or road, because there is no way to obtain consent from all affected users.
A small accessory building less than 4.5 metres from a street boundary therefore requires a building permit; it is not covered by the permit exemption.
The ruling does not decide whether a permit should be granted; the specific building’s eligibility for an after-the-fact permit must be assessed.
outcome: MÖD upheld the finding that the playhouse was not exempt from the permit requirement and that its eligibility for a permit must be assessed.
source: MÖD 2013:18 (P 105-13, 2013-06-07): Tillsynsåtgärd avseende komplementbyggnad

question: I want to establish a mussel farm in a sheltered sea inlet near Makrillskär in Lysekil, within the shoreline-protection area. The farm must be placed in the water, and a sheltered location is important for mussel growth; a suggested location outside the protected area is more exposed and may conflict with shipping. The installation could affect recreational boating, and there are other mussel farms in the area.
key_points: A dispensation requires special reasons under MB 7 kap. 18 b §, and only the grounds listed in MB 7 kap. 18 c § may be considered.

Under MB 7 kap. 18 c §, a water-dependent facility may qualify when its need cannot be met outside the protected area; the court treated a mussel farm that must be in the water as covered by this ground.
The assessment considered the difficulty of finding another suitable location, including the need for shelter and the limited suitability of proposed alternatives.

The farm's impact on public recreation was limited, and it was not expected to substantially alter conditions for plant or animal life; the court also considered its positive effect in counteracting eutrophication.
The dispensation was time-limited and applied only to the specified project area.

evidence.contains: för sin funktion måste ligga vid vattnet och behovet inte kan tillgodoses

outcome: MÖD granted a time-limited shoreline-protection dispensation for the mussel farm, valid through 31 December 2018.
source: MÖD 2013:22 (M 8456-12, 2013-06-04): Strandskyddsdispens för musselodling

question: I own a holiday home in Herresta, Strängnäs, for which the municipality granted a building permit in 1996 for an extension and a garage; the permit was valid until October 2001. The house’s main structure was in place before the permit expired, but I completed further work, including the exterior and windows, afterwards. The detailed plan limits the main building to 100 m² and one storey, while the 1996 permit allowed a small deviation. Do the later works need a new permit, and can they be approved?
key_points: Work carried out in accordance with a valid building permit during its validity period is not reassessed in a later permit review.
Only work not completed before the permit expired, or work that departed from the permit, requires a new building-permit assessment.
The new assessment must address the additional works, rather than reassessing the entire building volume already covered by the valid permit.
Where the record does not establish which works were done after expiry, the municipality must investigate those works before deciding whether a permit can be granted.
A building charge cannot be based on permitted work, and the authority must identify the unauthorized work on which the charge rests.
outcome: MÖD set aside the refusal and sent the permit matter back for investigation of which works were done after the original permit expired, and it also overturned the building charge.
source: MÖD 2013:24 (P 8920-12, 2013-05-31): Bygglov och byggnadsavgift

question: Can I build two new residential buildings in an existing courtyard area in Majorna, joining them to buildings on neighbouring plots? The area has older wooden residential buildings and lies within a culturally sensitive part of the city that is also designated a national cultural-environment interest. The applicable 1878 stadsplan shows the block boundaries but contains no rules on building placement or height; the project would increase overlooking and reduce daylight for nearby homes.
key_points: An old stadsplan that remains in force is not obsolete merely because it contains few or no detailed building rules; it continues to apply until amended or repealed.

Under the transitional rule in 17 kap. 4 § ÄPBL, 39 § byggnadsstadgan applies as a plan provision where the old plan does not provide otherwise; the court found no conflict with its distance rules or a height limit.
Under 3 kap. 1 § ÄPBL, placement and design must suit the townscape and cultural values; a detailed cultural-environment description supported the finding that the design was appropriately adapted.
Under 3 kap. 2 § ÄPBL, overlooking and reduced daylight are assessed in context; the court found the resulting nuisances were not significant given the character of the area.
outcome: MÖD dismissed the appeals and left the building permit in force, finding the project compatible with the applicable plan and building requirements.
source: MÖD 2013:17 (P 9167-12, 2013-05-23): Bygglov i stadsdelen Majorna i Göteborg

question: I am planning to abstract groundwater from wells on the Kristianstad Plain to irrigate agricultural land. The wells would draw from an important aquifer that is also used, or may be used, by other water users, and there is uncertainty about future groundwater recharge and the effects of climate change. Could I obtain a permit for this abstraction, and for how long?
key_points: Under MB 16 kap. 2 §, a permit may be time-limited; the circumstances of the individual case must warrant that restriction.
MB 1 kap. 1 § requires water to be managed for long-term ecological and socioeconomic sustainability, relevant where the aquifer is important and shared.
Under MB 2 kap. 3 §, the operator must take the precautions needed to prevent harm; uncertainty about recharge, climate change and long-term effects may support a limited permit term.

MB 11 kap. 7 § requires water operations not to obstruct future activities affecting the same water resource; the court also weighed competing users and changing agricultural land use against the applicant’s investment and planning interests.

evidence.contains: används så att en från ekologisk
alla som bedriver eller avser att bedriva en verksamhet
så att den inte försvårar annan verksamhet som i framtiden
tillstånd, godkännande eller dispens enligt balken eller enligt föreskrifter

outcome: MÖD upheld the permit for groundwater abstraction for agricultural irrigation but limited its validity to 25 years from the date the judgment became final.
source: MÖD 2013:39 (M 5301-12, M 5298-12, 2013-05-06): Tidsbegränsat tillstånd för uttag av grundvatten för jordbruksbevattning

question: I want to develop land near Albovägen in Staffanstorp for housing beside existing villa properties. The proposed plan relies on stormwater detention within the development area, including a ditch or other storage, but it is unclear whether the municipal water and wastewater service area also covers stormwater or who will be responsible for ensuring the solution is built and maintained. Some neighbouring villa owners could voluntarily acquire adjoining land, and the plan does not settle the future property division.
key_points: Under ÄPBL 5 kap. 7 §, a detailed plan may regulate only the matters authorized by that provision; the stormwater-flow condition used here lacked statutory support.
ÄPBL 5 kap. 8 § allows certain conditions to be imposed before building permits, but neither ÄPBL nor PBL allows the permit process to compel the specific stormwater solution described in this plan.
Under ÄPBL 5 kap. 9 § third paragraph, the plan documents must make clear how the plan regulates the environment, including the material prerequisites for stormwater handling.
When stormwater management is decisive to implementation, the plan must clarify how it will be handled and who will ensure the detention solution is implemented and maintained.

The consequences of implementation must be foreseeable and satisfactorily resolve conflicts between new and existing development; a land-allocation agreement or possible future property-formation proceedings did not cure the plan’s deficiency.
outcome: MÖD dismissed the municipality’s appeal, leaving in place the decision to overturn adoption of the detailed plan because stormwater handling had not been secured.
source: MÖD 2013:14 (P 5128-12, 2013-04-10): Upphävande av beslut om antagande av detaljplan

question: Can I develop a vacant site of about 3,400 square metres in Åkarp with a three-storey apartment building of around 30 flats and associated parking? The site is at the corner of Alnarpsvägen and Lundavägen, next to a school and near residential villas. Åkarp has recurring stormwater-capacity problems, and the plan says runoff must be delayed and limited to 1.5 litres per second per hectare; the area identified for a proposed stormwater storage facility is restricted to sheds and garages, and the plan does not set a minimum plot size.
key_points: Under ÄPBL 2 kap. 3 §, land must be suitable for its intended use, including with regard to water conditions and the ability to arrange water and sewage.
ÄPBL 5 kap. 7 § exhaustively limits what may be regulated in a detailed development plan; it did not authorize requiring the specified stormwater installation through a building-permit condition.
ÄPBL 5 kap. 9 § third paragraph governs how plan documents are presented and does not independently authorize a stormwater plan provision.

The municipality must clarify in the plan documents that stormwater can be managed; a plan that lacks plot-size rules may allow subdivision before building, undermining reliance on a shared stormwater solution.
A proposed stormwater facility must also be compatible with the plan’s land-use provisions; the proposed facility was in an area where only sheds and garages were permitted.
outcome: MÖD set aside the decision adopting the detailed development plan because the municipality had not clarified in the plan that stormwater could be managed acceptably, and the plan could not require the specified stormwater solution to be provided at the building-permit stage.
source: MÖD 2013:20 (P 2699-12, 2013-04-10): Upphävande av beslut om antagande av detaljplan

question: I want to make a preschool that has operated for about 20 years in Tannefors permanent through a detailed plan. It would use an existing building currently designated for housing, surrounded by other homes, with no new building proposed. Saab operates an airport nearby under a permit for up to 50,000 aircraft movements per year, and aircraft noise affects the area.
key_points: Under 1 kap. 5 § and 5 kap. 2 § ÄPBL, a detailed plan must balance public and private interests and account for existing development that may be affected.

A plan encroaches on an operator’s permitted industrial interest only if its implementation can be expected to affect the operator’s ability to conduct activities under the current permit in an unreasonable way.
For noise-related suitability, a preschool location is normally assessed in the same way as housing; the court found no reason to impose stricter requirements on a preschool.
Using an existing building already surrounded by homes did not risk expanding development in a way that would harm Saab’s private interest in continuing and developing its permitted operations.
outcome: MÖD rejected Saab’s appeal, leaving the detailed plan for the preschool in force.
source: MÖD 2013:48 (P 3664-12, P 3666-12, P 4259-12, 2013-02-28): Detaljplaner angående förskoleverksamhet respektive bostäder samt förhandsbesked för enbostadshus

question: Can we get a detailed plan adopted for a horse-sports arena on a roughly 70-hectare rural site near Vara, with accommodation and facilities for around 50–100 permanent horses and up to 400 visiting horses? The surrounding area includes agricultural land, and the wider area being considered is about 500 hectares. Two alternative sites nearer Vara and the E20 were considered but set aside because land matters were thought difficult; moving the facilities within the area has also been discussed.
key_points: Under MB 6 kap. 12 §, reasonable alternatives must be identified, described and assessed in light of the plan’s purpose and geographical scope.
For a land-use plan, reasonable alternatives can include other locations for the planned type of activity.
The alternatives must be presented in enough detail for decision-makers and the public to compare their environmental effects with the selected option.
Stating only that alternative sites were studied and land matters were difficult does not suffice; the plan material must identify the alternatives and explain why they were rejected.

evidence.contains: Rimliga alternativ med hänsyn till planens eller programmets syfte

outcome: MÖD annulled the municipality’s decision to adopt the detailed plan because the environmental impact assessment did not adequately identify and explain the alternatives that had been considered and rejected.
source: MÖD 2013:9 (P 4149-12, 2013-02-26): Antagande av detaljplan

question: Can a detailed plan for Svinningeudd allow conversion of an established mixed holiday-home and permanent-residence area into a larger residential area, with about 50 additional homes among roughly 77 existing developed properties? The area is about 10 km from Åkersberga, local roads have long been managed by property-owner associations, and other plans in the wider Svinninge area provide for private responsibility for public places. The proposal provides for municipal water and sewerage and municipal responsibility for the main collector road, but private responsibility for local roads and other public places.
key_points: Under the applicable ÄPBL, the municipality was normally to be responsible for public places in a detailed-plan area; private responsibility required special reasons.

Special reasons may be supported by the area’s distance from the urban centre, its established road-management arrangements, the absence of municipally operated facilities, limited opposition from residents, and private responsibility in neighbouring plans.
A limited expansion that preserves the area’s mixed holiday-home and permanent-residence character can support private responsibility for public places.
Municipal water and sewerage and municipal responsibility for a main collector road do not by themselves require the municipality to manage local roads.
outcome: MÖD set aside the lower court’s judgment and upheld the decisions adopting the Svinningeudd detailed plan, including its private responsibility for public places.
source: MÖD 2013:3 (P 3775-12, P 7100-12, 2013-01-30): Upphävande av beslut om antagande av detaljplan

question: I want to demolish the existing house and build a new single-family home with a carport and storage building on my plot in a densely built coastal area, in the third row of properties from the sea. The detailed plan allows building on the plot, and the proposed buildings would extend along part of a boundary; the neighboring property has a veranda with a limited sea view, and properties closer to the sea also have unused building rights. Could this project be permitted despite its effect on the neighbor’s view?
key_points: Under PBL 2 kap. 9 §, a building’s placement and design must not cause significant nuisance to the surrounding area, even when the project complies with the detailed plan.
Assess nuisance in light of all circumstances, including the character of the area, local conditions, and the building rights allowed by the detailed plan.
A property owner is not guaranteed a permanent sea view; in a built-up area with properties in rows, substantial obstruction may have to be accepted.
Consider how much of the view was realistically available before the project and whether development of intervening properties under their existing building rights could also obstruct it.
The permit covers the building as a whole, so the carport and storage building could not be assessed separately from the rest of the permitted project.
outcome: MÖD dismissed the appeal and upheld the building permit, finding that the loss of the neighbor’s sea view was not a significant nuisance in the circumstances.

question: I own a 3,507 m² plot in Nacka with a one-storey house of about 80 m² and an already-built two-storey extension of about 45 m². The extension does not comply with the current plan, but the municipality has endorsed a proposed new detailed plan that would provide sufficient building rights for it. Only an implementation agreement with the local road association remains before the plan is expected to be adopted; can I keep the extension and obtain a permit afterward?
key_points: Under the former PBL enforcement rules, the authority may defer corrective action when it is likely that the unauthorised work can receive a permit afterward.
That principle can apply even when the current plan does not allow the work, if a plan amendment is sufficiently likely to create the necessary building rights.
An advanced plan proposal, endorsed by the municipal committee and expected to be adopted soon, supported the likelihood of a future permit in this case.
Setting aside a demolition order does not itself grant a building permit; the ruling addressed whether demolition should be ordered at that time.
outcome: MÖD set aside the demolition order because the advanced plan work made it likely that the owner could obtain a permit for the extension afterward.
source: MÖD 2012:52 (P 1368-12, 2012-11-22): Rivningsföreläggande för tillbyggnad

question: Can the municipality amend a detailed development plan for an area outside Krokom’s town centre so that responsibility for public places, including roads, shifts from the municipality to private management? The existing plan, adopted in 1989, covers an area planned for both permanent homes and holiday homes, and most of the housing is permanent. Neighbouring areas have private management, and the municipality wants uniform management across the municipality; no other changes to the plan are proposed.
key_points: Under ÄPBL 6 kap. 26 §, the municipality is to be the principal for public places unless special reasons justify another arrangement.
A municipality cannot simply relinquish responsibility for public places; the special-reasons requirement is intended to prevent it from doing so without adequate justification.
A wish for uniform management across the municipality, without explaining the circumstances underlying that policy, is not by itself a special reason to change a long-standing arrangement.
The plan amendment changed only who was responsible for public places, and no changed circumstances in the area or municipality were identified.
outcome: MÖD dismissed the municipality’s appeal, leaving in place the decision to annul the plan amendment because the stated wish for uniform management was not a special reason to change the long-standing municipal responsibility.
source: MÖD 2012:44 (P 8115-12, 2012-11-20): Upphävande av beslut om antagande av detaljplan

question: I own a house on Stora Dyrön in Tjörn, in a densely built-up area with small plots and buildings close together. The house has an existing balcony above an extension permitted in 1961, and I want to enclose the balcony as part of an alteration that increases the living area. The 1957 plan marks the plot as non-buildable and its provisions do not allow additions or extensions.
key_points: Under ÄPBL 8 kap. 11 §, a building-permit measure within a detailed plan must comply with the plan unless a qualifying minor deviation can be allowed.
A detailed plan must be applied until replaced; its age or perceived obsolescence does not justify a more flexible interpretation.
Where the plan prohibits additions, the proposed alteration is plan-inconsistent even if it does not enlarge the building footprint.

The minor-deviation assessment must consider the proposed work together with deviations previously accepted; the resulting increase of at least 21 m² in building area and 33 m² in gross floor area was not minor.
Without a plan amendment, building permission could not be granted for this measure.
outcome: MÖD overturned the earlier decisions and refused building permission because the alteration contravened the plan and the combined deviation was not minor.
source: MÖD 2012:43 (P 3502-12, 2012-10-29): Bygglov för ombyggnad av enbostadshus

question: I want to build a holiday house near the shore at Gärsnäs by lilla Värmeln, in Grums municipality, about 50 metres from an existing home. The municipality’s 2010 comprehensive plan identifies the area as a LIS area, but the county administrative board objected that the mapped area was too large and needed better justification. Can I obtain a shoreline-protection exemption for the house?
key_points: Under MB 7 kap. 18 e §, a LIS area must be suitable for rural development and limited in character and extent so that shoreline-protection purposes remain safeguarded in the long term.

An översiktsplan is guidance, not binding; where the municipality and county administrative board disagree about the LIS designation, the plan does not create a presumption that the statutory criteria are met.

The applicant must provide enough support for finding that the area can promote rural development over the long term while accounting for shoreline-protection purposes; general claims about local spending or service are insufficient.

For a single home, its own contribution to rural development cannot establish that the site is in a LIS area; the proximity of an existing home is relevant to the exemption ground in MB 7 kap. 18 d § only if the site is within a qualifying LIS area.

evidence.contains: lämpligt för utvecklingen av landsbygden
uppföras i anslutning till ett befintligt bostadshus

outcome: MÖD held that the site had not been shown to lie in a qualifying LIS area and upheld the decision to revoke the shoreline-protection exemption.
source: MÖD 2012:39 (M 10239-11, 2012-10-18): Strandskyddsdispens med tillämpning av 7 kap. 18 d-e §§ miljöbalken

question: I want to build two detached houses on grass or pasture land in the Vareslätten area north of Himlevägen, outside a detailed development plan. Four houses have already been built on land subdivided from the same larger property, in two groups beside the site; I would place one new house beside each group and leave the area between them open. The municipal comprehensive plan says the area should mainly be used for agriculture, calls for great restraint on new building except for agriculture, and says new buildings should be near existing ones; I consider the land unsuitable for cultivation or livestock.
key_points: Under ÄPBL 8 kap. 34 §, a preliminary ruling examines whether a building requiring a permit can be allowed at the proposed location, including the site’s suitability for the intended use.
The comprehensive plan is not binding under ÄPBL 1 kap. 3 §, but it guides decisions on land and water use and sets out relevant public interests.
The balancing of private and public interests takes place in the individual application under ÄPBL 1 kap. 5 §; the municipality has broad discretion in shaping the built environment.

Here, the public interest in agricultural land use and the plan’s policy of great restraint outweighed the applicant’s interest in building, even though the proposed houses would be beside existing homes.
outcome: MÖD overturned the lower court’s judgment and upheld the municipality’s refusal of a positive preliminary ruling for the two houses.
source: MÖD 2012:40 (P 4799-12, 2012-10-18): Förhandsbesked för enbostadshus utanför detaljplanelagt område

question: Can the municipality use the simplified planning procedure for a plan allowing apartment buildings in Njurundabommen? The site currently has a detailed-plan designation for public use and contains a church office; the proposed plan would allow housing and increase the permitted building area from 450 to 2,000 square metres. The site is mostly within 100 metres of the shoreline, and shoreline protection was lifted under the existing plan; the area is designated for housing in the local in-depth comprehensive plan.
key_points: Under the then-applicable ÄPBL 5 kap. 28 §, simplified planning procedure was available only when the plan was of limited significance, lacked public interest and was consistent with the comprehensive plan and the County Administrative Board’s review statement.
Changing land use from public purpose to private housing can be of broader public interest, even if the site is already covered by a detailed plan.
The increased building rights did not, by themselves, make the plan too significant for simplified procedure in this case.

Under MB 7 kap. 18 g §, shoreline protection that had been lifted through the earlier detailed plan re-entered when that plan was replaced; the new plan therefore needed to address the shoreline-protection issues.
The decision concerned the choice of planning procedure, not whether housing could ultimately be permitted through a properly conducted normal procedure.
outcome: MÖD quashed the adopted plan, finding that the change from public to private residential use, the increased building rights and the shoreline-protection context meant the plan should have been handled through the normal planning procedure.
source: MÖD 2012:42 (P 3242-12, 2012-10-01): Detaljplan för bostäder

question: I own a property in Värmdö within a shoreline protection area and have already blasted and excavated to make a road because the existing slope makes access difficult. The road is on my property, but some rock removal may have affected the neighboring property, and the drawing submitted with my application did not show that boundary issue. Can I obtain a retroactive strandskyddsdispens for the work?
key_points: A strandskyddsdispens is assessed by reference to the public interests protected by the shoreline rules; private interests and the precise property boundary do not determine whether the dispensation may be granted.
A strandskyddsdispens means only that the shoreline rules do not prohibit the specified measure; it does not give the applicant a civil-law right to carry out work on another person's land.
MB 24 kap. 3 § governs revocation of permits; alleged errors about the boundary did not justify revocation here because they did not affect the public-interest assessment.
Neighbors need not be consulted on a strandskyddsdispens application, and a neighboring landowner does not gain appeal rights merely because the proposed measure affects their land.
outcome: MÖD dismissed the municipality’s appeal, holding that it could not revoke the granted retroactive dispensation based on the alleged misleading boundary information, so the dispensation remained in force.
source: MÖD 2012:33 (M 6657-11, 2012-09-10): Återkallelse av beslut om strandskyddsdispens

question: Can the building committee adopt a detailed-plan amendment for a retail area in Lund that removes unused building rights from a 1989 plan? The plan’s implementation period has expired, and the proposed amendment would limit further retail expansion while traffic solutions are studied. The plan area is limited in size, is not a sensitive environment, and does not conflict with state interests.
key_points: Under the delegation rule in 5 kap. 29 § ÄPBL, the municipal council is the default decision-maker, but may delegate plans that are neither of a principled nature nor otherwise of major importance.
Whether a plan is of major importance must be assessed in context; substantial economic consequences for the landowner do not alone make it so.
The amendment’s limited area, lack of sensitivity, and absence of conflict with state interests supported adoption by the building committee.
The amendment removed unused building rights while the municipality awaited further traffic planning; the court found no other circumstance making the plan principled or of major importance.
outcome: MÖD upheld the building committee’s adoption of the plan amendment, finding that it had not exceeded its authority.
source: MÖD 2012:35 (P 3003-12, 2012-08-30): Antagande av detaljplan

question: I want to build a detached house in Hjortnäs, in Leksand, on part of the open Sturåkern field. The land is part of a larger agricultural landscape and is cut for silage, and the area is designated as a national interest for nature and cultural values. Can I obtain a förhandsbesked for the house?
key_points: After a remand, an inferior authority should normally accept the superior court’s assessment of the case; this follows from the nature of the court hierarchy.
A new assessment after remand may be justified by new evidence or circumstances, or by a manifest error in the superior court’s assessment.
The earlier courts were considered to have assessed whether the proposal was compatible with the protection of valuable agricultural land under MB 3 kap. 4 §.
Because no exception to the remand rule applied, the county administrative board could not reassess the site’s suitability and the positive förhandsbesked stood.
A förhandsbesked is a preliminary decision on whether the proposed location may be suitable; it is not itself a building permit.
outcome: MÖD upheld the positive förhandsbesked, ruling that the lower authority had to accept the earlier courts’ assessment and could not reopen the substantive suitability question.
source: MÖD 2012:54 (P 2884-12, 2012-08-29): Förhandsbesked för bostadshus

question: I want to redevelop the former Centralgaraget site in Johanneberg, Göteborg, with housing, retail and services in three buildings: two nine storeys high and one 17 storeys high. The area has older functionalist buildings and is identified as a national cultural-environment interest; the proposed tower would be visible from large parts of the city. The comprehensive plan broadly marks the urban area for development with green and recreational spaces, but does not specify this density or where landmarks should be placed. Can the building committee adopt this detailed plan under delegated authority?
key_points: Under the delegation rule in former PBL 5 kap. 29 §, the municipal council adopts detailed plans; it may delegate only plans that are neither of principle nor otherwise of major importance.
The proposed 17-storey landmark, its visibility across the city, and the plan’s effects on the townscape made this plan one of major importance.
The comprehensive plan’s broad designation of the urban area did not provide concrete support for the proposed development, affecting the assessment of whether adoption could be delegated.
The ruling addresses the authority to adopt the plan, not whether the proposed buildings are substantively suitable; adoption by the appropriate municipal body remains a separate matter.
outcome: MÖD upheld the annulment of the plan, finding that it was of both principle and major importance and therefore could not be adopted by the building committee under delegated authority.
source: MÖD 2012:31 (P 8591-11, 2012-08-13): Detaljplan för bostäder och handel

question: I want to extend our existing treatment home in Enköping, which operates as a home for care or residence (HVB). The extension would add six resident rooms and supporting facilities; residents stay for several months, but treatment is the main purpose of the operation. The 1966 town plan, which applies as a detailed plan, allows the area to be used only for residential purposes.
key_points: Under the then-applicable ÄPBL 8 kap. 11 §, a building permit within a detailed-plan area generally required the measure to comply with the plan.
Whether an operation fits a plan’s use provision requires an overall assessment of the operation’s nature and the environmental effects it may generate.
Although an HVB home combines care or treatment with accommodation, the decisive issue here was that treatment—not residence—was the operation’s principal purpose.
A minor-deviation exception cannot be used to permit land use for a purpose not contemplated by the plan.
outcome: MÖD quashed the building permit because the extension was for a treatment operation rather than residential use, contrary to the detailed plan, and this was not a permissible minor deviation.
source: MÖD 2012:25 (P 15-12, 2012-07-05): Ansökan om bygglov för tillbyggnad av hem för vård eller boende (HVB-hem)

question: I want to build a rectangular house with a wide dormer and habitable rooms in the attic on a coastal plot in Trelleborg. The detailed plan allows a one-storey dwelling with a maximum building height of three metres, and the proposed house would be within the area designated for building. Its south-facing long side fronts the public beach, while the opposite side faces an area where building is prohibited.
key_points: Under ÄPBL 8 kap. 11 §, a building permit in a planned area required the proposal to comply with the detailed plan, subject to the exception for minor deviations compatible with the plan’s purpose.

Under PBF 9 §, the selected facade and the 45-degree roof plane determine the building-height calculation; the court used the beach-facing facade and found a height of five metres against the plan’s three-metre limit.
A two-metre excess in building height was not a minor deviation that could be accepted under ÄPBL 8 kap. 11 §.
Under PBF 9 §, an attic with habitable rooms counts as a storey when the height test is met; the proposed attic therefore made the dwelling two storeys, although the plan permitted one.
The extra storey was also not a minor plan deviation, so the permit could not be granted.

evidence.contains: till skärningen mellan fasadplanet och ett plan

outcome: MÖD revoked the building permit because the house exceeded the plan’s permitted building height and storey count, and neither deviation was minor.

question: I own an established estate beside a lake in Höör, with a main house and other existing buildings. I want to build a garage with guest accommodation within the shoreline-protected area; on the north side, there is a cleared opening and a small shore area that appear to have been used with the estate since around 1975, and the house is visible from that area. No tomtplats has previously been formally determined for the existing buildings. Can I obtain a shoreline exemption, and how much of the existing grounds may be included in the tomtplats?
key_points: Under MB 7 kap. 18 f §, a shoreline-exemption decision must state how far land may be taken as a tomt or used for the intended purpose.
A tomtplatsbestämning made with an exemption for a new accessory building may cover existing buildings and other land not directly affected by the application when no earlier determination exists.
The authority must assess the overall land use and whether the new measure would extend the privatized area enough to prevent an exemption.
A tomtplats boundary identifies the extent the owner may take as a tomt; it does not determine the full reach of allemansrätten or the home-frid zone.
The boundary must be assessed case by case, considering the buildings, public passage, nature interests and the proportionality of any burdensome conditions.

evidence.contains: i vilken utsträckning mark får tas i anspråk som tomt

outcome: MÖD upheld the lower court’s decision, including its tomtplats boundary for the cleared northern shore area and its rejection of further enlargement.
source: MÖD 2012:24 (M 1260-12, 2012-06-26): Tomtplatsbestämning i samband med strandskyddsdispens

question: I want to build about 80 homes and two roads in the Ekerum area of Borgholm, as part of a larger development planned for about 300 homes. The development areas are immediately next to the Halltorp Natura 2000 site, where protected beetles depend on sunlit oaks and other broadleaf trees. One area is a narrow wooded corridor that connects the protected site with potential habitats in nearby areas; the plans would require removing some trees and placing homes close together.
key_points: Under MB 7 kap. 28 a §, a Natura 2000 permit is required for a plan or project that may affect the protected site, including development outside its boundary.
Under MB 7 kap. 28 b §, permission requires that the project cannot damage protected habitats or significantly disturb protected species.
Effects on species’ dispersal routes outside the Natura 2000 site can count as disturbance when those routes are important to the species’ survival within the site.
The assessment must consider whether the development, alone or together with other projects, could impede the conservation of the protected species and their favourable conservation status.
Permission is available only when the best scientific knowledge leaves no reasonable doubt that the project will not have a harmful effect.
outcome: MÖD overturned the lower court’s decision and upheld the refusal of a Natura 2000 permit for the housing areas and roads.
source: MÖD 2012:34 (M 9438-11, 2012-06-20): Tillstånd enligt 7 kap. 28a § miljöbalken

question: I want to add a wing at right angles to my detached house in a residential area of Göteborg. The house’s south long side faces a nearby road, and its north side faces neighboring gardens. The detailed plan limits building height to 4.5 metres, but allows a greater height if the building committee considers it suitable in view of the height of the existing building; my proposed extension includes a roof ridge higher than that limit. Can I obtain building permission for the extension?
key_points: Under 8 kap. 11 § ÄPBL, a project within a detailed-plan area must comply with the plan unless the deviation is minor and consistent with the plan’s purpose.
Under 9 § ÄPBF, building height is calculated from the average ground level by the building and to the roof intersection defined by the 45-degree measurement rule.
For this building, the south long side facing the nearby road was the reference facade for calculating building height.
The calculated height exceeded the plan’s 4.5-metre limit by 2.6 metres, which was not a minor deviation eligible for approval.
outcome: MÖD overturned the building-permission decision, finding that the 2.6-metre excess over the plan’s height limit was not a minor deviation.
source: MÖD 2012:30 (P 7834-11, 2012-05-28): Bygglov för tillbyggnad av enbostadshus

question: Can I get a building permit for a garage and conservatory on my property in Råå, Helsingborg, where area regulations allow garages at the boundary with a neighbouring plot but there is no detailed development plan? The neighbourhood is densely built, with joined houses and enclosed streets. The proposed construction would stand by my neighbour’s house, where a small, high window is the only source of daylight to the kitchen area of a larger room; that room has two other windows elsewhere.
key_points: Under 3 kap. 2 § ÄPBL, a building must be located and designed so that it does not cause significant nuisance to people nearby.
Area regulations allowing a garage at the boundary do not give the owner an individual building right or rule out a nuisance assessment.
The nuisance assessment considers the area’s character and local conditions; the dense, joined development in Råå means some loss of light may need to be tolerated.
A substantial loss of daylight to a central part of a neighbouring home can nevertheless amount to significant nuisance, even where the affected window is small and high.
When balancing the neighbours’ interests, the interest in a garage and conservatory may yield to the need to preserve sufficient daylight in the neighbouring home.
outcome: MÖD overturned the lower courts’ decisions and revoked the building permit because the construction would cause significant nuisance by substantially reducing daylight to the neighbour’s kitchen.
source: MÖD 2012:16 (P 6567-11, 2012-05-25): Bygglov för garage och uterum

question: I own an older house in Helsingborg, next to a similar house, in an area with varied facade materials. The house’s brick facade and balconies are in poor condition, and I want to add new exterior cladding for repair and insulation, change some window openings, and alter the balconies. The detailed plan does not prohibit the changes, and the property has no formal conservation designation or area preservation programme.
key_points: For alterations, ÄPBL 3 kap. 10 § requires work to be carried out carefully, taking account of the building’s character and safeguarding its relevant values.
Under ÄPBL 3 kap. 12 §, a particularly valuable building may not be distorted; formal designation as a listed building or protection in a detailed plan is not required.
ÄPBL 3 kap. 1 § requires suitable design in relation to the townscape and local natural and cultural values, and an aesthetically pleasing exterior form and colour.
Under ÄPBL 1 kap. 5 §, public and private interests must be weighed; the ruling did not determine the final permit outcome.
outcome: MÖD set aside the lower court’s ruling and remitted the case to that court for continued proceedings, without deciding whether the building permit should be granted.
source: MÖD 2012:13 (P 285-12, 2012-04-26): Bygglov för fasadändring

question: I want to build two wind turbines on land in Mellerud municipality, within an area of national interest for military total defence associated with Såtenäs airfield. The Armed Forces considers that the turbines could seriously affect the airfield and opposes the project.
key_points: Under ÄPBL 13 kap. 4 §, a court must refer a case to the Government when it concerns an issue of special importance to the Armed Forces.
The special-importance test covers general suitability questions about locating buildings or activities that may affect the use of defence facilities.
A building-permit application for wind turbines in an area where the Armed Forces opposes the establishment meets that test.
Referral to the Government determines who will examine the matter; this ruling does not decide whether the permits should be granted.
outcome: MÖD quashed the lower court’s decision and referred the case to the Government because the application raised an issue of special importance to the Armed Forces.
source: MÖD 2012:8 (P 1397-12, 2012-03-23): Överlämnande till regeringen för prövning av ansökan om bygglov

question: I want to change land in Simrishamn from parkland to two additional residential plots beside existing homes. The current detailed plan designates the area as public parkland, and the comprehensive plan describes it as a recreational park area. The land is part of an existing jointly managed facility for park and planting, and it is also subject to an older public-space designation.
key_points: Under ÄPBL 1 kap. 5 §, planning must take account of both public and private interests; when private interests conflict, the municipality must carefully weigh them and explain why one outweighs the other.
Under ÄPBL 5 kap. 2 §, a plan must give reasonable consideration to existing ownership and property arrangements that may affect implementation.

A detailed plan changing jointly managed parkland to housing must adequately investigate the necessary reconsideration of the existing joint facility and explain the implementation consequences for affected owners.
The effects of any existing public-space designation under 113 § of the Building Act must be addressed when considering whether the land can be used for housing.
outcome: MÖD upheld the decision to annul the detailed plan because the municipality had not adequately considered existing property arrangements or explained how the competing private interests should be balanced.
source: MÖD 2012:14 (P 9691-11, 2012-03-16): Antagande av detaljplan i Simrishamns kommun

question: Can I transfer about 7,400 m² of forest land within the strandskydd area by Hasselasjön to my existing residential property, which is about 1,860 m²? I want the land mainly as a protective zone against logging and to improve the living environment, and I do not plan to change how the forest is used.
key_points: Under FBL 3 kap. 1 §, each affected property must be permanently suitable for its purpose, considering its location, size and other conditions.
Under FBL 3 kap. 1 §, a purpose that should instead be met in another way cannot justify fastighetsbildning.

A wish to create a protective zone against logging is generally not, by itself, a sufficient reason to add forest land to a residential property; the court referred to the consideration rule in 30 § skogsvårdslagen.

The court found the conditions unmet for the area outside the indicative tomtplats, but remitted the matter for Lantmäteriet to assess whether a more limited transfer corresponding to that area should proceed.

evidence.contains: varaktigt lämpad för sitt ändamål
bör tillgodoses på något annat sätt än genom fastighetsbildning

outcome: MÖD set aside the earlier decisions and remitted the matter to Lantmäteriet, finding the need for a protective zone insufficient to justify transferring land outside the indicative tomtplats while leaving a possible transfer within that area for further investigation.
source: MÖD 2012:36 (F 8328-11, 2012-03-05): Fastighetsreglering

question: I want to build a holiday cottage on a rural plot in Åre, near a small stream cut into a shallow ravine. The stream has little water at times and may dry up during summer; an existing holiday cottage is less than 50 metres from my plot, and there are subdivided plots along the access road. The land is connected to a farm that has belonged to my family for a long time.
key_points: Under MB 7 kap. 13 §, shoreline protection applies at watercourses as well as at the sea and lakes; a small stream may qualify even if it sometimes has little water.
The relevant assessment is whether the feature is a watercourse in the meaning of the Environmental Code; seasonal low flow or occasional drying does not alone exclude shoreline protection.
Under MB 7 kap. 18 c §, dispensation requires special grounds from an exhaustive list and must be consistent with shoreline protection’s purposes.
A wish to build a holiday cottage and personal attachment to the place are not, by themselves, special grounds; nearby buildings and plots do not change that assessment.
outcome: MÖD dismissed the appeal and refused shoreline-protection dispensation, finding that the seasonal stream was a watercourse and that there were no special grounds for an exemption.

question: Can I get a positive preliminary decision to build a single-family house on land in Borås that is covered by a detailed development plan? The proposed site is about 80 metres north of a nearby car-painting business; the plan says the implementation period for this land starts only once the business’s solvent emissions fall to 0.5 tonnes per year, and the business still uses more than that amount. There are other homes closer to the business, and I have lived nearby without noticing odours or discomfort.
key_points: Under the applicable older PBL rules, a detailed development plan may specify a later start for its implementation period; here the plan had gained legal force and tied that start to the business’s solvent emissions.
Because emissions remained above the plan’s stated threshold, the implementation period had not begun; MÖD applied ÄPBL 8 kap. 11 § as an obstacle to granting building permission.
A negative preliminary decision was therefore appropriate under ÄPBL 8 kap. 34 §; the nearby homes, distance, wind direction and reported lack of odour did not change that conclusion.
MÖD questioned whether the plan provision met legal requirements for clarity and predictability, but did not resolve that issue because the plan had gained legal force.
outcome: MÖD upheld the refusal of a positive preliminary decision because the detailed plan’s implementation period had not begun, creating an obstacle to granting building permission.
source: MÖD 2012:29 (P 6568-11, 2012-01-31): Förhandsbesked för nybyggnad av enbostadshus

question: I own land by Mälaren in Sigtuna, where a path used by the public runs along the shore toward an old landing stage. My house is far enough from the shore that the area is outside the normal residential plot, and I am considering removing soil by the path, leaving exposed rock and a steep section, and placing a large stone where the path enters my land. Would these works be allowed without a shoreline-protection dispensation?
key_points: Under MB 7 kap. 15 §, installations or arrangements that impede or deter public access to a shoreline-protected area are prohibited.

Works need not be conventional structures: the combined effect of soil removal, exposed rock, a steep section, and a placed stone can be comparable to the examples in the legislative preparatory works.
The public-access assessment matters where the area is otherwise freely accessible; the court noted that the shore was outside the property’s normal residential plot.
Where prohibited works lack a dispensation, the authority may require restoration; an order framed as enabling passage comparable to the previous situation can be sufficiently clear and appropriate.

evidence.contains: hindrar eller avhåller allmänheten från att beträda

outcome: MÖD upheld the order to restore the shoreline path, finding that the works were covered by the shoreline-protection prohibition and had no dispensation.
source: MÖD 2011:36 (M 2082-11, 2011-10-06): Föreläggande enligt miljöbalken att vidta åtgärder för att återställa strandpromenad på fastigheten Haga-Kumla 1:5 i Sigtuna kommun

question: I own a developed property on an island in Värmdö, with a house, a shore-side outbuilding and an older concrete pier that cannot safely be used for boat access because it is near a busy shipping lane. I want to build a floating pier of just over 50 square metres, with a walkway and deck, in the water beside the property. The nearby shallow seabed has stone and sand and supports bladderwrack, and the area is valued for nature and outdoor recreation; the proposed site lies between the property and a public ferry pier.
key_points: Under MB 7 kap. 13 §, strandskydd protects public access for outdoor recreation and good living conditions for plants and animals on land and in water.
Under the applicable older wording of MB 7 kap. 16 §, a structure is prohibited if it deters public access or substantially worsens conditions for plant or animal species.

A site is not considered already taken into use for purposes of the exemption merely because the shore is developed; the water area and accessible areas beside the property remained relevant to the protection.
A large, visible pier could deter the public and harm vegetated seabed; in a heavily exploited archipelago, even local impacts may contribute to significant ecosystem fragmentation.
MB 7 kap. 18 § requires special grounds for a dispensation; here the pier’s function could be met through ferry transport or a smaller pier, so no special grounds were established.

evidence.contains: på land och i vatten
hindrar eller avhåller allmänheten från att beträda ett område
om det finns särskilda skäl

outcome: MÖD overturned the lower court’s judgment and upheld the county board’s refusal to grant strandskyddsdispens for the pier.
source: MÖD 2011:29 (M 5649-10, 2011-08-31): Strandskyddsdispens
